title: Saving Spaces wipes extension enablement, site permissions, grants and folders
description: SQLiteTabRepository.saveSpaces does SpaceRow.deleteAll then re-inserts. extensionEnablement, grantedPermission, sitePermission and folder reference space ON DELETE CASCADE, and credential.lastUsedSpaceId is ON DELETE SET NULL, so any Space change (add, rename, reorder, delete -> TabStore.persistSpaces) silently wipes every Space's enabled extensions, extension grants, site permission decisions and folders in the DB, and clears credentials' last-used Space. In-memory state hides it until the next launch. Found 2026-10-30: after adding a Space, all four tables were empty in the user's DB (16 site permissions in the 2026-10-26 backup). Fix: differential save (update existing rows, insert new, delete only removed Spaces), test that child rows of surviving Spaces survive a save. Then restore the user's rows (enablement for Personal: ddkj, nngc, ponf from logs; sitePermission from Backups/chord.sqlite.20261026-123005.bak).
close_reason: e23eed7: differential saveSpaces + regression test (fails on old code). User data restored 2026-10-30 11:10: Personal enablement (ddkj, nngc, ponf) from logs, 16 sitePermission rows from the 2026-10-26 backup; pre-restore copy in Backups/pre-restore-20261030-111040. Not recoverable: grantedPermission (extension grants), folders (backup had none), site permissions set after 10-26, Kerja enablement (no load ever logged).

title: Extension bundles install without signature verification
description:
ExtensionInstaller.swift:46-64 installs any .crx/.xpi/.zip by stripping the CRX header (ExtensionArchive.swift:67) and writing the ZIP to disk; the CRX2/CRX3 signature is never validated and unsigned .xpi/.zip install with no provenance. Anyone who opens a malicious bundle runs its code with full extension privileges. WebKit provides no signing store, so the browser must check.

DECISION (2026-08-07): trust model is WARN-BUT-INSTALL. Unknown or missing signer is not blocked; the UI shows an unverified-developer warning before the bundle is enabled. Verified signatures from a pinned key are trusted silently. No paid Apple signing identity required.
design: Verify CRX2/CRX3 signatures against a pinned public key (store key or developer key); unknown/missing signer is allowed but flagged in the UI before enable. .xpi/.zip carry no signature, so they always take the warn path. Reuse ExtensionArchive byte parsing; keep bundle load path unchanged. Surface verification result (verified / unverified) on the extension row and in an install-time confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: CRX2/CRX3 signatures are actually verified against a pinned public key (not stripped-and-ignored); unsigned .xpi/.zip and unknown-signer bundles still install but the UI shows an unverified-developer warning at install and on the extension row, and they are not silently trusted; tampered bundles are detected and flagged; tests cover tampered, unsigned, valid, and unknown-signer bundles
close_reason: CRX2/CRX3 signatures verified at install in new BrowserCrypto package; warn-but-install UI (row icon, install message, enable confirmation); verdict persisted as <slug>.verification; 10 verifier + 4 installer + 3 UI tests; prepush green

title: Blank tabs: in one Space every new load is cancelled by a second, page-initiated navigation that Chord ignores
description:
Seen twice: 2026-10-30 evening (test Spaces after a force-kill; wrongly blamed on sqlite edits) and 2026-10-31 04:37-04:45 in Space 3 (7B9DDE4F...) of the instance launched right after the c1k.12 crash. Other Spaces in the same instance loaded fine (Space 4). A relaunch cleared it (04:46); not persisted.

WebKit log for one blank tab (pageProxyID=735, 04:39:38): loadRequest navigationID=741, policy Use, provisional load starts; 3 ms later the WEB PROCESS starts another main-frame load (FrameLoader::load (FrameLoadRequest), decidePolicyForNavigationAction navigationID=0 -> 743), which cancels 741 (-999, willInternallyHandleFailure=1); Chord's decidePolicyFor navigationAction answers 743 with policyAction=Ignore; the page is left as the empty initial document. Every tab in that Space did this (Wikipedia, example.com, example.net); reload did nothing visible.

Unknown: the URL of the second navigation (private in WebKit's log) and which NavigationCoordinator branch cancelled it (needsNewView/extension page, Peek, or the UA re-issue — the re-issue logs a new loadRequest, none seen, so likely needsNewView+!mayOpen or Peek). Suspects for a page-initiated load at document start: a document-start user script (c1k.3 bundle, ChromeWebStoreRelay, PasswordFormMonitor) or an extension content script in that Space (Bitwarden nngceckbapebfimnlniiiahkandclblb, uBlock Lite ddkjiahejlhfcafbddmgiahcphecmpfh). Next: temporary DEBUGNAV logging in NavigationCoordinator (url, source frame, navigationType per cancel branch; AppLog lines are public) and repro: kill -9 Chord with a Space open, relaunch, open a tab there.
notes: 2026-10-31 04:52: the PERSISTENT part is fixed in dbab1f2: the blank tabs had saved an empty interaction state (paneInteractionState.data 137 bytes vs 676 for a real page), and revive restored it instead of loading pane.url, so they stayed blank across relaunches (kill -9 + relaunch reproduced it). LiveWebView.restore now returns backForwardList.currentItem != nil and the engine loads the URL otherwise. STILL OPEN: why, in one Space of one session, every new load was cancelled by a page-initiated second navigation that NavigationCoordinator ignored. A Release build with DEBUGNAV logging (url, source frame, navigationType per cancel branch) was running at 04:51; not reproduced since (graceful relaunch and kill -9 relaunch both load fine now).
close_reason: Both parts fixed: dbab1f2 (empty saved history restored instead of loading) and b76d317 (uBOL strict-block DNR redirect rules match every site in WebKit, b/298199; shim leaves them out). Repro loop 3/6 blank -> 0/6.

title: Idle CPU: background pages keep running their own timers (37-43 ms/s vs Safari 4-9)
description: 2026-10-30 tab-set re-run (BASELINE doc, evening section): with Chord's own timers gone (c1k.5) and churn fixed (c1k.9), idle CPU is still 37-43 ms/s; hidden, two WebContent processes take 9.9 and 8.3 ms/s. Safari 4-9. Find which pages (map pid to tab: Develop menu / log the web process pid per pane), then compare what Safari does for the same page hidden: WebKit's hidden-page timer throttling, inactiveSchedulingPolicy (.suspend for long-hidden tabs?), occlusion propagated to WKWebView (window occluded -> views hidden), page visibility state. Measure with scripts/perf-baseline.sh idle 300 + per-pid cputime from the plist.
notes:
2026-10-31 05:20: committed 87adcce — WKPreferences hiddenPageDOMTimerThrottlingAutoIncreases (Safari on, apps off; checked with a probe: default 0). Hidden, paused, ps cputime: YouTube 16.3+9.8 -> 9.2 ms/s, Chord total ~48 -> ~26 (docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-10-31-c1k11.md; not perfectly controlled). Still to do: a powermetrics tab-set run to confirm; the remaining YouTube 9 ms/s (sample shows DOMTimer + microtask JS, JSON.parse leaf; check whether Chord's YouTubeAdBlocker 2 s backup tick / MutationObserver or Bitwarden's content script contributes — try with extensions off); Safari side-by-side for the same hidden YouTube page. Note: GPU process ~43 ms/s while a video plays hidden; the tab-set script's YouTube autoplays, so verify paused via log 'pauseInternal'.
2026-10-31 06:45 A/B (docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-10-31-c1k11.md): paused hidden YouTube ~11 ms/s per tab in Chord with or without Chord's YouTube script and with or without extensions; Safari 0 ms/s because it SUSPENDS the hidden page's process a few minutes after hiding. Chord uses inactiveSchedulingPolicy=.throttle for tabs deliberately (music, chat sockets). DECISION FOR USER: switch tabs to .suspend (Safari behaviour; WebKit keeps audio-playing pages alive regardless) — maybe except pinned/favourite tabs or tabs that showed a notification — or keep .throttle. The 87adcce auto-increase is worth ~3 ms/s at 5 min. Harness: scratchpad abrun.sh (protocol) + playing.sh (pid last media event); pause verification must use the log.
2026-10-31 08:10: 332899f adds Settings > General > Background Tabs 'Suspend tabs you can't see' (default ON = inactiveSchedulingPolicy .suspend; off = .throttle; live views re-stamped). Hidden steady state: YouTube ~0, Chord ~10 ms/s (was ~45; Safari baseline 4.4). Left: (1) powermetrics tab-set run to confirm (needs the user's password); (2) a Bitwarden worker start calls into every tab (scripting.executeScript, Code=7 per tab) -> WebFrame_GetFrameInfo wakes every suspended process; the c1k.9 hold limits it to the first minute or two; (3) cpu.sh counts Safari's WebKit processes too when Safari is open — filter by Chord's coalition if reused.
2026-10-31 09:15 powermetrics tab-set run (Release 332899f, suspend ON, videos paused; raw in scratchpad pm-results.txt): a) front CPU 32.6 / wk 799 (UI 714) / energy 32.1; b) hidden 18.1 / 58 / 34.6 (WebContent energy 31.8 = ~9 short-lived processes from the per-ping pinger page -> fixed in b1c0cf5, NOT yet re-measured); c) minimized 18.0 / 865 (UI 851, 13.5 ms/s) / 7.3. REGRESSION FOUND: with tabs .suspend, parked (isHidden) tab pages get RemoteLayerTreeDrawingAreaProxy::hideContentUntilPendingUpdate when their process suspends and never complete -> UI runs WebKit display links (~375-850 wakeups/s, ~12 ms/s UI CPU) in front and minimized; not when app hidden (UI 4.3). Same mechanism as c1k.10 but on tabs. NEXT: (1) re-measure with b1c0cf5 (churn gone?); (2) decide: default the toggle OFF, or find a way to suspend without the spin (e.g. remove parked views from the window while suspended / only suspend when the window isn't visible); compare totals suspend-on vs off with cpu.sh (filter Chord's pids: cpu.sh also counts Safari's WebKit processes).
2026-11-01 07:20 (Release b1c0cf5, wk/ps harness, no powermetrics): the display-link spin is NOT caused by the suspend toggle. Suspend ON: front 95 UI wk/s (13 ms/s), minimized 598 (24 ms/s), hidden 249. Suspend OFF: front untouched 13-14/s but after re-activating 736 (total CPU 39), minimized 971 (37), hidden 59 (24). Cause (log): every window state change (activate, minimize, occlusion) sends SetActivityState to every page in the window; parked (isHidden) tabs' processes wake (Background), then ~3.5 s later WebKit suspends them again (prepareToSuspend -> RemoteLayerTreeDrawingAreaProxy::hideContentUntilPendingUpdate, never completed) and the UI runs WebKit DisplayLinks until the next wake. Happens with .throttle too: idle hidden processes are suspended either way. Safari has no parked views in the window. FIX in progress: WebSurfaceContainerView removes a parked web view from the window after 30 s parked (frame kept, re-added at container bounds on unpark, skipped while fullscreen).
2026-11-01 07:50: detach fix (uncommitted, AnyWebSurface.swift + 2 tests) measured. Run 1 (a video still playing): minimized UI 14.6 wk/s, hidden 12 (were 598-971). Run 2 (clean, nothing playing): front 12-16 wk/s for 5 min, then at ~07:36 a spin to 855/s that stayed. lldb breakpoint on RemoteLayerTreeDrawingAreaProxyMac::didRefreshDisplay: 7 drawing areas firing every frame = exactly the 7 parked tabs, ALREADY OUT OF THE WINDOW. So detaching stops the window-state wakes but a detached page still spins once something else wakes it and it re-suspends. The 07:36:55 wake: an extension service worker started (WebPageProxy::loadServiceWorker) and every parked tab process took a Foreground assertion within 0.3 s (worker start calls into every tab, the known Bitwarden scripting.executeScript Code=7 path; Code=7 errors also logged every 5 s). Spin onset at ~07:36:26 not yet explained. NEXT: stop extension calls reaching parked/suspended tabs (or batch them), then re-measure; scratchpad ba29ef79.../probe.sh + states.sh + wk + lldb.cmds.
2026-11-01 09:20: out-of-window parking dropped: a detached parked page still spins once woken after suspension, and out of the window WebKit suspends it even under .throttle (08:35 run). ROOT CAUSE (WebKit, not Chord): WebProcessProxy::sendPrepareToSuspend calls hideContentUntilPendingUpdate on every page, which sends DispatchAfterEnsuringDrawing (forced rendering update); when the process suspends before that commit completes, the UI's RemoteLayerTreeDrawingAreaProxy keeps a pending DisplayDidRefresh and its DisplayLink observer fires every frame (~120/s per page) until the process next runs. Any wake of a suspended parked tab (window activate/minimize/occlusion change, extension worker start calling into every tab, ...) re-arms it. .throttle does NOT prevent suspension on macOS 27. .none: 0 suspensions in 15 min, UI 12-15 wk/s front, 8 minimized, 6 hidden; total CPU 29/34/48 ms/s (hidden WebContent ~10-15 per paused YouTube) vs suspend-on with spin ~30/24/16 ms/s but 580-860 wk/s. COMMITTED: toggle off = .none. DEFAULT left ON pending user decision. Follow-ups: report the WebKit bug; consider Bitwarden worker restart cascade (hold renew).

title: Chrome-style host access: installing is the yes, in every Space
description: User asked (2026-10-30) after seeing access sheets: other browsers never show them. Chrome asks once at install. Now every installed extension (incl. ones added before Chord's install question) gets its manifest sites at load in every Space; enable no longer prompts. The page-access question (1mm.17) remains a safety net for optional requests. Known: switching off all-sites access in a Space still comes back on relaunch (denials aren't persisted) — as before for consented installs.

title: Extension page-access questions stack up and repeat
description: User report 2026-10-30: with no site grant, Bitwarden queued one sheet per open tab's site, asked again right after Don't Allow, and re-asked for sites already allowed; 'quite annoying if I need to always press Allow'. Fix: an extension whose manifest (incl. optional host permissions) asks for every site is asked once for *://*/*; a question already up absorbs repeats; Don't Allow holds for the session; already-granted URLs are answered without a sheet.

title: Allowing an extension on a page grants only that exact URL, so it asks again on every page
description: WKWebExtensionControllerDelegate promptForPermissionToAccess urls (WebKitExtensionHost ~line 1724): on Allow, Chord stores kind=url with the full page URL including query (seen: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=..., reddit ?solution=...&jsc_token=...). The next video or page is a different URL, so the extension asks again on every page; user report 2026-10-30 ('every extension always ask permission when opening new web'), visible once the broad grants were wiped by ls5. Chrome/Safari ask per site. Fix: on Allow, grant the site (scheme://host/* match pattern, fenced via ExtensionGrants) and persist that as matchPattern; keep Don't Allow per site for the session. Also consider offering 'Allow on all sites' when the manifest asks for all hosts. Tests: allow on one URL, a second URL on the same host is not prompted; another host is.

title: WebContent process churn: one process started and torn down every ~25 s
description: c1k.1 baseline: in every 5-minute Chord phase (in front, hidden, minimized) 12 WebContent processes in Chord's coalition started and exited, mean life ~27 s, i.e. one launch every ~25 s; Safari 2-4 per phase. Only 3 long-lived WebContent processes served the 10 tabs, so these are not tabs. Hypothesis: an MV3 extension worker (Bitwarden or uBlock Lite, enabled in 2 Spaces) is revived by Chord and then unloaded by WebKit's idle timer, over and over; the 25 s period matches the native-port keep-alive (cc13ebf: native ports send a 25 s keep-alive) and the worker-revive path (1mm.6.x). Work: confirm by counting launches with extensions off vs on and per extension (powermetrics coalition via scripts/perf-baseline.sh idle 300, then the churn snippet in BASELINE doc), find the reviver, stop waking an idle worker unless an event needs it. Accept: churn <= Safari's (<=4 per 5 min) with Bitwarden+uBlock enabled in 2 Spaces, and Bitwarden still unlocks/autofills; re-run idle rows a-c.
notes: 2026-10-30: cause = Bitwarden (signed out / no native port) 1-min alarm + WebKit 30 s idle unload -> new WebContent per wake per Space (experiments: uBlock-only Spaces 0 new procs/3 min; Bitwarden in 2 Spaces 6/3 min). Fix committed (adaptive keep-alive via hidden-page __chordPing; native-port traffic does not keep a worker loaded; shim stamp fingerprint so shim changes reach installs). Live: one restart at ~1 min then held, no further churn over 4 min. Left: re-run baseline idle rows a-c (powermetrics, sudo) to quantify; then close.
close_reason: Re-measured idle a-c after 4190e0c: energy 108/82/123 -> 18.7/31.9/15.7; new WebContent processes per 5 min 12 -> 1-2 (each Space's Bitwarden restarts once per 10-min hold). CPU unchanged (38-46 ms/s) - long-lived page processes, c1k.5. Numbers in docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-10-30.md 'After c1k.9'.

title: Cross-origin-isolated pages (COOP+COEP) load blank
description: Found by c1k.1: every https://browserbench.org/Speedometer3.1/ tab in Chord stays blank white; the tab title stays the host (document never commits), reload doesn't help, nothing in Chord's log. Safari loads the same URL. The response has Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin + Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp, i.e. cross-origin isolated, which makes WebKit swap to a new WebContent process (browsing-context-group switch) for the navigation. Something in Chord's view setup breaks that swap. Suspects: NavigationCoordinator.decidePolicyFor re-issuing the request for the user agent (cancel + webView.load) interacting with the process swap; the configuration template (inactiveSchedulingPolicy, extension controller, user scripts in a COEP page); the pool/parked surface. Repro: open https://browserbench.org/Speedometer3.1/ in a new tab (Release build, a Space with uBlock+Bitwarden; also try a Space with no extensions). Fix, then add an E2E test with a local server sending COOP/COEP headers, and fill Chord's Speedometer row in docs/perf/BASELINE-2026-10-30.md (3 runs, median).

Added CrossOriginIsolationTests (local COOP+COEP server: fresh tab, after another page, with an extension controller; crossOriginIsolated true). title: perf.6: Stop every progress tick redrawing the sidebar and RootView (PaneRuntime.apply sets all fields)
description:
SYMPTOM (verified by reading the code, 2026-10-29): every KVO tick of ANY pane, for example estimatedProgress firing many times during a load, invalidates every SwiftUI view that reads ANY PaneRuntime field of THAT pane. That includes the sidebar rows, PinnedList/PinnedGrid, and RootView's body itself.

WHY: Swift Observation (@Observable) notifies on every property SET, even when the new value equals the old one. Nothing checks for equality.

THE CHAIN:
1. ChordEngine/WebViewPool.swift ~lines 69–74: LiveWebView KVO-observes title, url, isLoading, estimatedProgress, canGoBack and canGoForward. Each change runs refreshSnapshot() (~line 124), then onChange → WebKitEngine.handleSnapshot (WebKitEngine.swift ~line 1546) → delegate.paneDidUpdate.
2. ChordStore/TabStore.swift ~line 1789, paneDidUpdate → `runtime(for: paneID).apply(snapshot)`.
3. ChordStore/PaneRuntime.swift ~line 44, apply(_:): it assigns ALL TEN fields unconditionally (isLoading, estimatedProgress, canGoBack, canGoForward, currentURL, isPlayingAudio, isMuted, sleepTimerDeadline, isScreenSharing, loginForm). So a progress tick also "changes" isPlayingAudio, isMuted, sleepTimerDeadline, isScreenSharing and loginForm.
4. Readers of those "unrelated" fields:
   - ChordUI/Sidebar/SidebarView.swift ~lines 177–179 and ~420–422: the TabRowView arguments read isPlayingAudio, isMuted and sleepTimerDeadline inside the ForEach in SidebarView's body. The whole SidebarView body re-runs, not just one row.
   - ChordUI/Sidebar/PinnedList.swift ~lines 31–33, PinnedGrid.swift ~line 83.
   - ChordUI/RootView.swift ~line 85: `sharingPaneID` reads isScreenSharing in RootView, the root of the window.
   - Toolbar/CredentialFillButton.swift ~line 31 reads loginForm.
   - Toolbar/NavigationBar.swift ~line 24 legitimately reads progress.
   The comment on PaneRuntime ("estimatedProgress ticking must not invalidate the sidebar") states the intent, but the unconditional apply defeats it.
Also: TabStore.runtimes is @ObservationIgnored (TabStore.swift ~line 528), so runtime(for:) creating entries doesn't invalidate anything. That part is fine.

FIX (small and mechanical; do it first):
1. PaneRuntime.apply: assign each field only when it differs:
   `if isLoading != snapshot.isLoading { isLoading = snapshot.isLoading }`, and the same for every field. Write a tiny generic helper if you like, for example `func set<T: Equatable>(_ kp: ReferenceWritableKeyPath<PaneRuntime, T>, _ v: T)`. Check that LoginFormAnalysis and Credential are Equatable (PaneSnapshot is Equatable, so its members are).
2. Coalesce estimatedProgress. WebKit can send 20–50 updates per load. Keep 0 and 1 exact, and drop changes smaller than 0.05 in between (or quantize to 1/20). Only NavigationBar's progress bar reads it.
3. Pass row inputs as values from a narrower scope. Make a small `TabRowAudioState` view that takes the PaneRuntime and reads the three fields inside its own body, so that only that row's subview is invalidated, not SidebarView. Same for PinnedList and PinnedGrid.
4. RootView.sharingPaneID: move the read into a small child view (the banner), so RootView's body doesn't depend on isScreenSharing.
5. Check the other high-frequency sources: the title (YouTube updates document.title for notifications) and the favicon. They go through the `tabs[index].updatePane` path in paneDidUpdate (~lines 1806+), which already guards with didChange, so verify that the guard really compares values.

HOW TO PROVE IT:
- Instruments > SwiftUI template > "View Body" and "View Properties" (Xcode 26/27), or temporarily add `let _ = Self._printChanges()` inside SidebarView.body and RootView.body (remove it before the commit).
- Load 5 heavy tabs at once and count SidebarView.body evaluations. Before the fix: dozens to hundreds per load. After: about 0 from progress, and 1 per real title or favicon change.

TESTS (ChordStoreTests):
- Use `withObservationTracking({ _ = runtime.isPlayingAudio }, onChange: { fired = true })`, then apply a snapshot that changes only estimatedProgress, and assert that fired == false.
- Same for isScreenSharing and loginForm.
- An apply that really changes isPlayingAudio does fire.
- Progress coalescing: 0.31 → 0.33 doesn't notify, 0.31 → 0.40 does, and → 1.0 always does.

DEPENDENCY NOTE: This doesn't need the full c1k.1 harness. An Instruments or _printChanges count before and after is enough proof, so start any time. c1k.1's CPU-during-load number is a bonus.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] A progress tick doesn't re-evaluate SidebarView, PinnedList, PinnedGrid or RootView (proved with Instruments or _printChanges, counts in the commit).
[ ] The new observation tests pass, and so does prepush.
[ ] No UI regressions: the audio icon, mute, sleep-timer badge, screen-share banner and fill button still update right away when their own state changes.

================ COMMON CONTEXT (same on every c1k.* task) ================
GOAL: Chord is a SwiftUI and AppKit browser on WebKit, the same engine as Safari. Raw page speed is therefore WebKit's. What Chord can win or lose is everything it adds on top: user scripts, extension controllers and workers, timers, SwiftUI redraws, and web views it keeps alive. The target is "no worse than Safari on the same tab set". Each task removes one of those added costs.

REPO MAP:
- Packages/Sources/ChordEngine: WebKit wrapper (WebKitEngine, WebViewPool, LiveWebView, the page user scripts *Monitor/*Bridge/*Controller).
- Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions: WKWebExtension host (WebKitExtensionHost, ExtensionShimScript = JS shim injected into every extension, ExtensionNative, ExtensionPopup).
- Packages/Sources/ChordStore: app state (TabStore, PaneRuntime, WindowState, ExtensionsService, AppEnvironment).
- Packages/Sources/ChordUI: SwiftUI views (RootView, Sidebar/*, Content/*, Toolbar/*).
- ChordApp/: the app target. Chord.xcodeproj builds it.
- Layering (ADR 011): ChordStore and ChordUI never import WebKit. They talk to extensions only through the `ExtensionHost` protocol (Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/ExtensionHost.swift). Every new protocol method needs a no-op default in the `public extension ExtensionHost` block (~line 160), so fakes and tests keep compiling.

BUILD / TEST / GATE:
- Build packages: `swift build --package-path Packages -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`. Warnings are errors.
- One test target: `/usr/bin/timeout 600 swift test --package-path Packages --filter ChordEngineTests --no-parallel`. Run one target at a time, and run `pkill -f swiftpm-testing-helper` between runs: ChordStoreTests sometimes hangs (bead x4b), so retry once before you suspect your change.
- The full gate before any commit is `scripts/prepush.sh`: package build, all tests, then the xcodebuild app build.
- Run the app: build the Chord scheme in Debug (`xcodebuild -project Chord.xcodeproj -scheme Chord -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build`) and open the .app from DerivedData.

LOGGING / MEASURING:
- Use `Log.<category>.notice("...")`, with the categories in ChordCore's AppLog. NSLog does NOT reach the unified log on this setup. AppLog has no `privacy:` argument.
- Read logs with `/usr/bin/log show --last 5m --predicate 'subsystem BEGINSWITH "app.chord"' --info`. Use the full path, because `log` is a shell function in the dev shell, and use `log show` because `log stream` exits early.
- Energy: `sudo powermetrics --samplers tasks,cpu_power -i 5000 -n 12` (it needs a human for sudo), Activity Monitor > Energy, Instruments (Time Profiler, SwiftUI, Energy Log, os_signpost).
- Every task records BEFORE and AFTER numbers with the c1k.1 harness (scripts/perf-baseline.sh once it exists) and puts them in the commit message.

RELEASE CONSTRAINT: Release CI builds against the macOS 26 SDK, while dev Macs have Xcode 27. `#available` only guards at run time, so any API that exists only in the macOS 27 SDK must be reached by name (NSClassFromString / KVC / perform). See `bd memories macos26` and PasswordFormMonitor.closedRootsWorld.

WORKFLOW RULES:
- `bd update <id> --claim` before you start.
- One task = one commit, which includes its tests. Message style: `Area: what changed, in plain words` (see git log). No Co-Authored-By or other attribution trailer.
- Don't push unless told to.
- After a commit, reindex codebase-memory (index_repository, mode full).
- `bd close <id>` with a short reason quoting the before and after numbers.
- If you find more work, file a new bead under epic c1k instead of widening the commit.
close_reason: Fixed in c05998c. The real cost was tabs[index].updatePane notifying every tabs reader on every snapshot, plus uncoalesced progress. PaneRuntime equal sets already skip notifying on this toolchain, so the task's main premise was half wrong. Proved with withObservationTracking tests; the tab-list test failed before the fix. No Instruments count taken.

title: perf.5: Kill forever-ticking timers (tabGroups poll, idle poll, popup sizing, YouTube tick)
description:
SYMPTOM: Repeating timers keep firing whether or not anything changed. Each one wakes a process, and some wake two of them through a native round trip. Fix each with an event, or stop it once it's no longer needed. One commit, five sub-fixes, each with its own test.

a) Shim tabGroups poll: Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/ExtensionShimScript.swift ~lines 1365–1394.
   NOW: the first addListener on chrome.tabGroups.onCreated/onRemoved/onUpdated starts `setInterval(groupsChanged, 3000)`. groupsChanged calls `native("tabGroups.query")`, which is a runtime.sendNativeMessage("chord", …) round trip to the host, diffs the result against `known`, and fires the events. It runs forever in every extension that listens, even when nothing changes.
   FIX: push. The host knows when groups change (TabStore folder and group operations → extension tab hooks in TabStore+Extensions.swift → WebKitExtensionHost). Options:
   (1) Long-lived port: at shim start (worker only), `runtime.connectNative("chord.events")`, the same way the shim already does "chord.socket" (~line 354). In ExtensionNative, keep the MessagePort for each context (the ports of a "chord.events" name, per context). title: perf.4: Background tabs never throttle — parked tabs stay visible in the ZStack; hide them + inactiveSchedulingPolicy
description:
SYMPTOM (strongly suspected; verify first): Background tabs never get WebKit's hidden-page throttling, so up to 12 tabs run timers, requestAnimationFrame, CSS animations and video decoding at full rate while the user looks at one tab.

CURRENT CODE (verified 2026-10-29):
- ChordUI/Content/WebContentCard.swift ~lines 26–46: every tab that has a live web view is mounted in a ZStack (`ForEach(mountedTabs)`) and stays mounted. Unselected tabs only get `.zIndex(0)`, `.allowsHitTesting(false)` and `.accessibilityHidden(true)`. They are NOT removed, NOT isHidden, and NOT opacity 0. The comment says why: detaching a WKWebView makes it rejoin at 0×0 and fire a resize that resets SPA state (the Instagram carousel bug). That reason still holds; the fix must not detach.
- The surface: ChordEngine/AnyWebSurface.swift. WebSurfaceRepresentable returns the LiveWebView.container (WebSurfaceContainerView). The web view is added with autoresizing (the workaround for fullscreen webkit.org/b/313802).
- Pool: ChordEngine/WebViewPool.swift. LRU with `capacity = 12` (init ~line 226), dropping to 6 or 3 under memory pressure (~lines 286–321). Under that cap, the live views are exactly the mounted tabs above.
- WebKit decides "visible" from the view's window and the hidden state of its ancestors (viewDidHide/viewDidUnhide, window occlusion). A view that is in the window and not hidden, only covered by a sibling, is treated as VISIBLE. That is the bug.
- Nothing in the codebase sets `inactiveSchedulingPolicy`. Check with grep -rn inactiveSchedulingPolicy Packages/Sources.

STEP 1: PROVE IT (commit nothing yet).
- Write a test page (data: URL or file) that every second logs `document.visibilityState`, `document.hidden` and the drift of a 100 ms setInterval (expected count vs actual) to the console, and shows them in the title.
- Open it in tab 1, switch to tab 2, wait 60 s, switch back, and read the log in Web Inspector. Expected bug: visibilityState stays "visible" and there's no timer clamping. In Safari the same page reports "hidden" and is throttled.
- Also check powermetrics on a background tab running a CSS animation, or a paused-but-animating site such as a news site with carousels.

STEP 2: FIX.
a) Hide without detaching. When a mounted tab becomes parked, set `container.isHidden = true` (or the web view's own isHidden) and set it back to false when it's selected. isHidden keeps the frame and the superview, so there's no 0×0 rejoin. Re-check the Instagram carousel case and fullscreen video. Where:
   - SplitContentView already gets `isParked` (ChordUI/Content/SplitContentView.swift ~lines 24/99). Pass it into the surface, for example through `store.surface(for:in:)`, or a modifier that reaches the NSView. updateNSView in WebSurfaceRepresentable is currently empty and can apply `nsView.isHidden = parked`.
   - The engine is the better owner. Add `WebEngine.setPaneVisible(_ paneID:, _ visible: Bool)`, called from TabStore.select, and have LiveWebView set isHidden itself. This also gives (b) one place.
b) inactiveSchedulingPolicy (WKPreferences, macOS 14+): for a parked tab, set `webView.configuration.preferences.inactiveSchedulingPolicy`:
   - `.suspend` when it isn't playing audio, screen sharing or in PiP;
   - `.throttle` otherwise. Use LiveWebView.isPlayingAudio / isScreenSharing and the PiP state the engine already tracks.
   Note: preferences are per configuration. If views share a configuration, setting this on one changes the rest. Check how configurations are made, since each view probably gets its own copy. If they're shared, set it at creation (.throttle) and rely on (a).
c) The foreground tab of each window must stay visible, including split-view panes: all panes of the selected tab are visible.
d) Re-check the pool cap: try 12, 8 and 6 with c1k.1 footprint and energy. Change it only if the data says so, and note that a lower cap means more reloads on tab switch.

PITFALLS:
- Background audio (YouTube, Spotify web) must keep playing under .throttle, so test it.
- PiP windows: a hidden source view must keep the PiP video going.
- Screen-share: the page that is sharing must not be suspended.
- The ephemeral sweep and the "recently used" behavior must be unchanged.
- Snapshots for the tab-switch animation or the sidebar preview (if any) may need the view unhidden. Grep for takeSnapshot.

TESTS:
- ChordEngineTests, with a real WKWebView in a real NSWindow: after setPaneVisible(false), `document.visibilityState` becomes "hidden" (poll for up to 2 s), and setPaneVisible(true) brings back "visible".
- A ChordStoreTests fake engine: selecting tab B calls setPaneVisible(A, false) and setPaneVisible(B, true).

[ ] The test page reports "hidden" in a background tab and its timers are throttled, matching Safari.
[ ] Background YouTube audio keeps playing. PiP keeps playing. Switching tabs keeps SPA state (the Instagram carousel stays on its slide) and fullscreen video still works.

description:

   - Space A: 6 tabs.
     - youtube.com/watch?v=<any 10-min video>, playing.
     - A second YouTube video, paused.

     - github.com/apple/swift (a repo page).
     - en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_browser (a long page).
     - A static page: example.com.

   - Safari: the same 10 URLs in one window with the same 2 extensions where they exist. Write down which ones.
2. Signposts in the app, which stay in afterwards for c1k.7 and c1k.8. Add these if they're missing:
   - Log.app.notice("perf launch") at the very top of app start (ChordApp init).
   - Log.engine.notice("perf first-paint <paneID>") the first time any pane's didFinish fires after launch. Use a static once-flag in WebKitEngine.
   - Log.engine.notice("perf tab-switch-start <tabID>") in TabStore.select.
   - Log.engine.notice("perf tab-switch-end <tabID>") when the newly selected pane's surface is visible. The simplest hook is the next main-runloop turn after the selection is applied; use a CATransaction completion if you need more precision.

3. scripts/perf-baseline.sh (bash, no dependencies beyond the macOS tools). Subcommands:
   - `startup`: quit Chord, launch it with `open -a`, wait 15 s, then parse the "perf launch" and "perf first-paint" times from log show. Repeat 5 times and print the median in ms.
   - `switch`: print the tab-switch median from the last 20 switch pairs in the log (a human clicks through the tabs, or use AppleScript/System Events to press Cmd-Opt-Down 20 times).
   - `idle <seconds>`: run powermetrics (needs sudo, so print the command and ask if it isn't root), filter to Chord + "com.apple.WebKit.*" processes whose parent is Chord, and sum "CPU ms/s", "Intr Wakeups/s" and "Pkg Wakeups/s".    - Each subcommand also takes `--app Safari` and attributes Safari's WebContent processes the same way.

   b) Hidden (Cmd-H), 5 min: the same metrics.

   d) Speedometer 3 (browserbench.org/Speedometer3.1), 3 runs, median, with no other tabs open.
   e) Cold start to first paint, median of 5.
   f) Tab switch, median of 20.
   g) Memory footprint by group, after (a).
   h) Count of live extension worker processes after launch. This is the c1k.2 baseline.
   End with "Biggest gaps vs Safari", ranked.
5. Paste the ranking into epic c1k's notes (`bd update webkit-arc-like-browser-c1k --append-notes "..."`), and change the priorities of c1k.2–8 if the data disagrees with the current order.

- Plug the Mac in, or keep it on battery, but use the SAME power state and brightness for both browsers. Close other apps. Let Spotlight indexing settle.

title: perf.2: Load extensions per Space lazily, not every Space at launch
description:
SYMPTOM: N Spaces × M enabled extensions = N×M background service workers, all started at launch, even in Spaces the user never opens this session. Each worker is its own JS heap, plus timers, plus native-messaging hosts. Bitwarden starts desktop_proxy, for example.

CURRENT CODE (verified 2026-10-29):
- One WKWebExtensionController per Space: WebKitExtensionHost.prepare(_ space:) (Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/WebKitExtensionHost.swift ~line 189) caches it in `controllers[space.id]`.
- Launch path: AppEnvironment.swift ~line 207 sets `store.afterRestore`, which calls `extensionsService.restoreEnabled(spaces: store.spaces)` (Packages/Sources/ChordStore/ExtensionsService.swift ~line 187). That loops over EVERY enablement record in every Space, calls `host.load(installed, in: space)`, and sleeps 400 ms after each extension that has a background worker.
- host.load (WebKitExtensionHost.swift ~line 301) → prepare(space) → WKWebExtensionContext → controller.load(context), which starts the worker.
- prepare(space) is also called ~line 1233, so that every web view of a Space references its controller from creation (WKWebViewConfiguration.webExtensionController can only be set at creation). An EMPTY controller is cheap. Keep that call.
- The active Space is per window: WindowState.activeSpaceID (Packages/Sources/ChordStore/WindowState.swift ~line 38). It is set from TabStore.selectSpace (TabStore+Spaces.swift ~line 19/48), TabStore+Windows.swift ~lines 93/178 and TabStore.swift ~lines 120/130/890.
- The per-Space model is a USER DECISION ("Keep per-Space"). Don't merge controllers across Spaces.

PLAN:
1. ExtensionsService: split restoreEnabled into
   - `restoreEnabled(spaces:, active: Set<UUID>)`, which loads only the records whose spaceID is in `active` (the union of activeSpaceID over all open windows);
   - `ensureLoaded(space:)`, which is idempotent: it loads the enabled records for that Space if they haven't been loaded yet. Keep a `loadedSpaces: Set<UUID>` in the service.
2. TabStore: when any window's activeSpaceID changes to a Space that hasn't been loaded yet, call a hook. Use one funnel instead of patching the five assignment sites: make `activeSpaceID` `didSet` call `store?.spaceBecameActive(id)`, or have the store observe it. The hook calls an injected closure `onSpaceActivated: ((Space) async -> Void)?`, which AppEnvironment wires to `extensionsService.ensureLoaded(space:)`. ChordStore already owns ExtensionsService, so this needs no new ExtensionHost method. If you do add one, give it a no-op default.
3. Content scripts for tabs that already exist when a Space loads late: the views already reference the Space's (empty) controller, and WebKit injects a context's content scripts into matching existing pages when the context loads. Verify this with a test extension that has a content script that sets document.body.dataset.cs = "1".
4. OPTIONAL second phase (a separate bead if it's big): idle sleep. Unload a Space's contexts after it has been inactive in every window for 30 min, then reload through ensureLoaded when it's activated again. Risks:
   - chrome.alarms set by the extension must still fire. WebKit persists alarms per context, so check after a reload.
   - Open native ports (desktop_proxy) must close cleanly. ExtensionNative handles disconnect.
   - Don't unload a Space that has an open popup or side panel, or a tab playing audio.
5. Update the host's `preparedSpaceIDs` users, if any assume that all Spaces are loaded.

PITFALLS:
- `loadedOnce` in WebKitExtensionHost (~line 1001) keys on "spaceID|identifier". Make sure lazy loading doesn't break the "first load in this Space" behavior: permission prompts are skipped on restore (ExtensionsService ~line 89).
- updateStoreExtensions(in: store.spaces) runs after restore and may call host.load for updated extensions in ALL Spaces (ExtensionsService ~line 141). Limit it to the loaded Spaces, and mark the others to pick up the update on ensureLoaded.
- Private windows have their own non-persistent Space (bead dlr.1 covers their teardown). Lazy loading must work for them too.
- Keep the 400 ms gap between workers inside one ensureLoaded call (WebKit fails workers that start at the same time).

TESTS (ChordStoreTests, with fakes from ChordTestSupport/Fakes.swift):
- restoreEnabled with 3 Spaces, 2 records each, and active = {A} → the fake host's load is called only for A's records.
- Activating B calls load for B's records exactly once, and activating B again doesn't load again.
- updateStoreExtensions only touches loaded Spaces.
- In a real host test (ChordExtensionsTests), the content script reaches a tab opened before its Space loaded.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] A fresh launch with 3 Spaces × 2 worker extensions runs only 2 extension worker processes (c1k.1 metric h).
[ ] The first switch to another Space has its extensions working (popup opens, content script present) within 1 s.
[ ] Bitwarden still unlocks and fills in a Space that was loaded late.
[ ] c1k.1 idle energy and the startup numbers, before and after, are in the commit message.
[ ] prepush passes.

title: Perf: as fast and power-efficient as Safari
description:
PURPOSE: Make Chord as fast and power-efficient as Safari, which runs the same engine. Measure first (c1k.1), then fix the costs Chord adds on top of WebKit, biggest first.

ORDER AND WHY (checked against the code on 2026-10-29):
1. c1k.1 Baseline harness. Nothing else can be judged without it. It blocks the others, except c1k.6, which is a verified, cheap bug that only needs an Instruments before/after.
2. c1k.4 Background tabs probably never throttle. Parked tabs stay mounted, unhidden, in a ZStack (ChordUI/Content/WebContentCard.swift), so WebKit sees up to 12 tabs (WebViewPool capacity) as visible and runs their timers, rAF and media at full rate. Likely the single biggest power cost.
3. c1k.6 Every load-progress tick of any tab invalidates the sidebar rows and RootView. PaneRuntime.apply assigns every field unconditionally, and @Observable notifies on every set, even when the value is equal.
4. c1k.2 Every enabled extension starts a worker in every Space at launch (N Spaces × M extensions).
5. c1k.5 Timers that never stop: shim tabGroups poll every 3 s, shim idle poll every 15 s, popup sizing every 250 ms, YouTube tick every 250 ms.
6. c1k.3 13 user scripts at document start. 11 of them go into every frame (ads included).
7. c1k.7 Startup: extension restore runs serialized, with 400 ms gaps, in the launch path.
8. c1k.8 Perf budget in prepush, so the gains stay.

title: Extension host never tears down a deleted Space or closed private window
description:
SYMPTOM
Deleting a Space, or closing a private window, removes the Space from the store and its tabs from the engine, but nothing tells the extension host. WebKitExtensionHost keeps, for the life of the process:
- controllers[spaceID]: the Space's WKWebExtensionController, with every extension still loaded in it. Their background service workers keep running; Bitwarden's keeps its desktop_proxy native host (ExtensionNative HostPipe) and its SignalR WebSocket (ExtensionSocket) open.
- dataStores[spaceID]: the WKWebsiteDataStore the controller uses. For a private Space this is a .nonPersistent() store (makeConfiguration(for:)), so a closed private session's extension cookies/storage stay in memory. The engine already fixed the same leak for its own store (WebKitEngine.removeData(for:) comment: "leaving it would keep a closed private session's cookies in memory").
- loadedContexts[spaceID], tabAdapters[spaceID], windowAdapters[spaceID], controllerSpace, spaces[spaceID], actionAnchors[spaceID], popouts[spaceID] (open extension popout windows), clearedWorkers, loadedOnce entries "spaceID|identifier", errorWatchers/revived entries keyed by the Space's contexts, the UserDefaults key chord.extensions.workers.<spaceID> (workersKey) and chord.extensions.settings.<spaceID>.<id> (ExtensionSettings, 1mm.13).
- WebKitEngine also keeps workerRecoveryAttachers[spaceID] and captureAttachers[spaceID] (closures from the host handle), never removed.

Likely second effect (VERIFY FIRST): for a deleted non-private Space, TabStore.deleteSpace then calls engine.removeData(for:) -> dataStores.removePersistentStore(dataStoreID:), i.e. WKWebsiteDataStore.remove(forIdentifier:). WebKit refuses to remove a store that is still in use, and the extension controller still holds WKWebsiteDataStore(forIdentifier: space.dataStoreID). If so, a deleted Space's website data is never reclaimed from disk. Confirm by deleting a Space with an extension loaded and checking the error log line "failed to remove data for space" (TabStore+Spaces.swift) or ~/Library/WebKit/<bundle>/WebsiteDataStore/<dataStoreID> still existing.

WHERE
- Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/WebKitExtensionHost.swift: state declarations near the top (controllers ... spaces), prepare(_:)/controllerHandle, makeConfiguration(for:), unload(slug:in:) (already does per-extension cleanup: error watcher, revived, closePopouts, offscreen close, side panel close, loadedContexts), forgetData(identifier:in:).
- Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/ExtensionHost.swift: the WebKit-free protocol + public extension with defaults.
- Packages/Sources/ChordStore/TabStore+Spaces.swift deleteSpace(_:in:); Packages/Sources/ChordStore/TabStore+Private.swift tearDownPrivateSession(_:). TabStore holds `weak var extensionHost: (any ExtensionHost)?`.
- Packages/Sources/ChordEngine/WebKitEngine.swift workerRecoveryAttachers / captureAttachers; removeData(for:).

FIX
1. Add to ExtensionHost: `func spaceDidClose(_ space: Space) async` (no-op default in the public extension).
2. Implement in WebKitExtensionHost: for each slug in loadedContexts[space.id], run the existing unload(slug:in:) path (so workers stop and offscreen/side panel/popouts/error watchers go); close remaining popouts; then drop every per-Space entry listed above (and the two UserDefaults keys only when the Space is deleted for good, not merely when a window closes on a persistent Space; private Spaces always). Drop controllers[space.id] last. Log one notice line.
3. Engine: drop workerRecoveryAttachers[space.id] / captureAttachers[space.id] in WebKitEngine.removeData(for:) (it already runs for both delete and private teardown).
4. Call it from TabStore.deleteSpace BEFORE engine.removeData(for:) (await it, so the data store is released first) and from tearDownPrivateSession inside the existing Task, before removeData.
5. Keep per-Space isolation: never touch another Space's controller.

ACCEPT
- Unit test (ChordExtensionsTests, real WKWebExtensionController like ExtensionAdapterTests): prepare a Space, load a minimal MV3 extension, call spaceDidClose; controllers/loadedContexts for that Space are empty (expose a DEBUG/internal count if needed) and another prepared Space is untouched.
- Store test (ChordStoreTests with RecordingExtensionHost): deleteSpace and tearDownPrivateSession each call spaceDidClose once with the right Space, before engine.removeData.
- Live: with Bitwarden enabled in a second Space connected to the desktop app, delete that Space: `pgrep -fl desktop_proxy` count drops; no "failed to remove data for space" log line. Open a private window, open Bitwarden popup, close the window: its controller is gone (temporary log).

title: Audit 2026-10-29: lifetime and leak findings
description:
Findings of a lifetime / leak scan of Chord on 2026-10-29 (main at 1c4be09), filed so other agents can fix them independently. Each child is self-contained: what is wrong, where, why it matters, how to reproduce or confirm, the fix, and acceptance.

Ranked by impact:
1. Extension host never tears down a Space (deleted Spaces, closed private windows): extension workers, native hosts, sockets and data stores live on until quit. Private-session data stays in memory.
2. Not every tab-removal path tells extensions (sweep, delete Space), and per-pane bookkeeping differs between the five removal paths.
3. ExtensionSocket has no orphan sweep, unlike ExtensionNative.
4. LiveWebView.tearDown cancels its own about:blank navigation and removes only some message handlers.
5. Window event monitors are not removed if their owner skips stop().

Checked and found sound (no task): WebKitEngine.forget(paneID:) clears every per-pane map; TabStore sweep loop holds self weakly; ExtensionNative HostPipe always reaches onExit so Live.pipes drains; ExtensionSocket/Popup/fullscreen KVO closures capture weakly; WindowRegistry holds windows weakly; per-view WKUserContentController means engine-lifetime handlers do not form a cycle with the view; memory-pressure source captures weakly and is cancelled in deinit; NSPanel selector observers are auto-removed.

title: Perf: PasswordFormMonitor rescans the whole DOM (and shadow roots) on every mutation
description: PasswordFormMonitor (Packages/Sources/ChordEngine/PasswordFormMonitor.swift) runs in every page. A MutationObserver on documentElement (childList, subtree, attributes incl. style/class) schedules report() at most every 150 ms; report() -> describe() -> collectInputs(document) does querySelectorAll('*') over the document and recursively every shadow root, then per input labelFor() (innerText -> layout) and isVisible() (layout), then JSON.stringify to compare. Pages that mutate constantly (YouTube Music progress/class changes, feeds, animations) pay this ~6-7x per second forever, including pages with no inputs at all. Measure (calls/s and ms/s per page), then cut: skip rescans when mutation records cannot affect inputs (no added/removed INPUT or shadow host, attribute changes not on/around tracked fields), cheap early-out for pages without inputs, keep correctness for shadow-DOM logins (Reddit) and fields unhidden by ancestors. Keep PasswordFormMonitor tests green; add tests for the skip rules.
acceptance_criteria: Measured before/after on a constantly mutating page (e.g. YouTube Music) and a login page; idle-page cost near zero; login detection tests green (incl. shadow DOM).
close_reason: Committed bb1f4ac. Facebook 10s: 35.5 scans/43ms -> 4.3 scans/1.3ms. YT Music 7.3/6.3ms, Slack 5.0/1.5ms after. E2E 48, Engine 77, Core 193 pass.

title: Perf: WebKit asks for background tabs' web views thousands of times
description: 2026-10-29 temporary log in ExtensionTabAdapter.webView(for:) (removed) counted ~1,000-1,900 nil answers per background (lazy/discarded) tab in one session, on the main actor, scaling with tab count. Something keeps WebKit enumerating tabs (tabs.query from extensions, windows tabs(for:) calls, or Chord re-reporting tabs). Find the caller (sample/Instruments or counted logging with a stack), cut the repeat cost (cache adapters, avoid redundant didChange* notifications, cheap nil path), measure before/after.

title: Folded sidebar stays out after an extension popup
description: Regression from d6147a2: presentAction/presentActionPopup set ExtensionPopup.onClose before show(); show() first calls close(), which fires and clears the new onClose, so 'popup closed' never reaches the window, WindowState.isExtensionPopupOpen stays true and the folded (auto-hide) sidebar never hides. Fix (uncommitted): WebKitExtensionHost.showPopup sets onClose after show and posts visible only if ExtensionPopup.shared.isUp.
acceptance_criteria: Folded sidebar hides on mouse-out after opening and closing an extension popup; also after opening one popup while another is open.
close_reason: Fixed in 0f69145; user verified folded sidebar hides.

title: Extension worker recovery: Bitwarden login needs a live worker port
description:
After the popup fix (f247903), Bitwarden's UI opens and renders. Logging in fails:

- 'Failed to unlock via master password' on a correct password. The stack lands on a null assertion (Gp), not a hash compare; next to it:
  'Invalid call to runtime.connect(). No runtime.onConnect listeners found.'
  'Invalid call to port.postMessage(). The port is disconnected.'
  So the popup's secure-messaging port never connects to the worker and Bitwarden reports it as a wrong password.
- After the email verification code, the flow spins forever; same port, plus
  'Unchecked runtime.lastError: Invalid call to tabs.create(). It is not implemented.'

WebKit does not queue runtime.connect until the worker registers onConnect (Chrome does) and does not restart a crashed MV3 worker. The reference browser solves this with a dedicated subsystem not yet ported:
- Sources/Search/ExtensionWorkerRecovery.swift (187 lines): watches WebKit's private _backgroundWebView, generation numbers, register/created/unregister, observe/cancel through native messaging and a webkit.messageHandlers bridge for content worlds.
- Sources/Search/ExtensionShims.swift lines ~1180-1300: worker generation stamping, passive port tracking with WeakRef/FinalizationRegistry, rewake on connect, keepalive.

Attempts so far: calling context.loadBackgroundContent before showing the popup made the popup paint blank; a shim-side connect-retry proxy was written but not verified and was reverted to keep f247903's working popup. main is clean at f247903.

Acceptance: with Bitwarden installed fresh, unlock succeeds with the correct master password, email-code login completes, and no 'No runtime.onConnect listeners found' appears in chord.log. Also implement chrome.tabs.create natively if the 2FA flow needs it.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-10-26 (worker recovery, phase 1).

Landed:
- ExtensionWorkerRecovery (ChordExtensions): per (Space, slug) generation + background lifetime; observes WebKit's private _backgroundWebView and the @objc didCreateBackgroundWebView delegate callback; registers before controller.load; unregisters/raises the generation on unload/reload; content-script bridge (chordWorkerRecovery, world WebExtension-<slug>, registered on every engine user content controller).
- Router: background.observe / background.unobserve (long-held reply, no 15s shim timeout).
- Shim: wraps runtime.connect + runtime.onConnect; tracks ports; on a new generation synthesizes onDisconnect (Chrome semantics) so the extension reconnects; keepalive on port traffic. Worker block is inert without a manifest background.
- Host: revive on WKWebExtensionContextErrorDomain backgroundContentFailedToLoad (same-context unload+load, max once/60s).
- Tests: 4 state-machine tests, 4 shim-worker JS tests, 3 router tests (212 ChordExtensions tests green). prepush green.

NOT yet verified: Bitwarden unlock + email-code flow on a real install (needs the app + extension; not possible from the CLI test run). Manual acceptance from the issue description still stands. tabs.create already landed in 4da9b0f.
FOLLOW-UP (same day): load now re-runs ExtensionShimInstaller.prepare when the sidecar fingerprint is stale, off the main actor, before WKWebExtension reads the bundle — so extensions installed before this build get the worker-recovery shim without a reinstall. title: Extension popup opens only once: use a Chord-owned popover like the reference
description:
User report: clicking the Bitwarden toolbar icon sometimes does nothing.

Reproduced in ChordTest with logs: the click reaches 'presentAction', WebKit reports action.presentsPopup=true and action.popupPopover != nil, but the presentation delegate is never called again after the first show. Instrumentation removed; commit 3debdf7 is the last state.

The reference browser does not use WebKit's popover at all:
  let url = action.popupWebView?.url ?? popupURL(for: context)
  action.closePopup()
  ExtensionPopup.shared.show(url, for: context, from: anchor(for: context.uniqueIdentifier))

It closes WebKit's popup, takes its URL, and presents its own NSPopover with a fresh WKWebView, so a second click is an ordinary new popover. Chord currently reuses action.popupPopover (WebKitExtensionHost.presentActionPopup), which appears to be single-shot.

Fix: port that shape — own popover (size to content, transient, Escape closes, anchor beside the extension button, per-Space), close WebKit's popup first, and keep the extension context so popup pages can use chrome.runtime. Add an XCUITest that opens the popup twice in a row (install a fixture extension with a popup; the store install stays manual).

Extension popups are Chord's own hidden-titlebar panel, opened from the manifest URL without calling performAction or didOpenTab; controller now gets an app-supplied webViewConfiguration; shim defines Symbol.dispose/asyncDispose. Inject a shim script into an installed extension (background worker, module worker import, every content script) and add the nativeMessaging permission it needs. The shim defines the Chrome APIs WebKit lacks and forwards calls as native messages to Chord, which answers natively.

title: [epic] Port selected reference-browser features into Chord
description:
Source: https://github.com/driceroland/Search (MIT, Swift/AppKit+SwiftUI+WKWebView, ~42k lines, one file per concern). Cloned at /Users/rizal/perkodingan/Search for reference. Feature-by-feature diff against Chord done 2026-10-25.

Contradicts two claims in our docs: (a) 'No passkeys. Not possible.' — Search carries the WebAuthn ceremony via ASAuthorizationWebBrowserPublicKeyCredentialManager + com.apple.developer.web-browser.public-key-credential (Apple grants on request; needs Developer ID provisioning profile). Already tracked as 40q. (b) 'MV3 password managers die on chrome.offscreen' — Search implements chrome.offscreen natively via a shim, so the class is not unfixable.

PHASE 1 — quick wins, no architecture change (~1 week, each independent):
- Copy Clean Link: strip utm_*/fbclid etc., keep unknown params + fragment, leave signed URLs alone. Replace existing Copy URL action.
- Tab discard/sleep: timer + reuse WebEngine.snapshot (already 'captures interactionState, tears the view down', WebEngine.swift:468) + isSleeping flag; keep tab, scroll, history. Distinct from archive/close.
- Media-key release: silence MPNowPlayingInfoCenter when media idle so Now Playing returns to other apps.
- Keyword shortcuts: 'yt cats' -> %s template, http(s) only.
- Address-at-rest: active tab shows registrable domain instead of title; flag punycode; needs eTLD+1 list.
- Settings search (find-a-setting), What's New card, AppleScript sdef (read-only tabs/URL/title), blocked-popup tray with per-site allow.
- Import: bookmarks HTML (Netscape) first; Arc StorableSidebar.json -> Spaces/pins second.

PHASE 2 — real features, no API risk:
- Reader mode (DOM prose heuristic, isolated world, reuse panel chrome).
- Site-search chips (prefix -> 'Search Reddit', OpenSearch discovery).
- Chromium password import (GRDB reads Login Data; decrypt with 'Safe Storage' keychain key).

PHASE 3 — extension layer (the one structural change; everything extension-related hangs on it):
- Unpack extension ZIP to a folder at install, inject shim.js into background worker + content scripts, add nativeMessaging permission, load folder via WKWebExtension(resourceBaseURL:). ExtensionInstaller currently keeps the ZIP and hands it to WebKit directly (ExtensionInstaller.swift:76).
- Shim subset only: chrome.offscreen, storage.session, privacy, minimal userScripts. Answer via native messaging. Unblocks Bitwarden/1Password class.
- Then, separately: Chrome Web Store install (port Crx.swift: CWS update endpoint + CRX3 id/signature check), native messaging hosts (unsandboxed app, so Process launch is fine), chrome-extension:// scheme instead of webkit-extension://.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS (evaluated, rejected):
- Passkeys: blocked on Apple-granted entitlement + Developer ID profile (see 40q).
- Apple Passwords / iCloud Keychain bridge: reverse-engineered OS protocol, breaks silently on macOS updates.
- Profiles: requires reworking TabStore/data root/keychain naming/per-Space extension controllers — multi-week persistence refactor.
- AI suite: Search ships it disabled (AI.shipped = false); needs signed helper process + hosted model; product decision.
- Floating video: we already have native PiP.
- Bench automation socket: port only open/wait/text/click/shot subset if E2E flakiness becomes real.
- Content blocking, YouTube ad skipping, Spaces: ours is stronger; keep.

METHOD: do NOT copy-paste — Search has no layered boundaries (one file per concern, everything imports WebKit). Extension work must stay behind ExtensionHost in ChordExtensions per ADR 011; budget +50% for extension items, +0% for UI/JS items.
design: Touchpoints: Engine (WebEngine.snapshot, page scripts, isolated world), Extensions (ExtensionInstaller ZIP->folder, shim injection, native messaging channel), Store (settings keys, tab isSleeping flag), UI (menus, settings sections), ChordCrypto (CRX3 verify, already present). No new third-party dependency; PSL list vendored or system.

description:
Safari 27 WebKit web-extension runtime now: (1) propagates user gestures through sendMessage/connect/postMessage/executeScript, so extensions can do media playback and other activation-requiring actions reliably; (2) reports uncaught JS exceptions + unhandled promise rejections in extension scripts; (3) adds runtime.getDocumentId().

Chord impact: per-Space WKWebExtensionController host (ADR 011). The gesture fix removes a whole class of 'extension action silently fails' bugs. The exception reporting feeds the ExtensionsPanel debugging story and directly addresses the 'popup spins forever / WKWebExtensionContextErrorDomain code 6' diagnosis pain in the chord-browser-maintenance skill.

Host is macOS 26.7 with Xcode 27 SDK (Safari 27 WebKit APIs run on macOS 26). One caveat: the new runtime surface (getDocumentId, exception reporting) should be probed at runtime on this build, since extension-runtime behavior can lag the WKWebView API.

Work: verify the new runtime surfaces on the macOS 27 SDK, surface extension-script errors in the extensions UI (ExtensionsPanel) / log, add getDocumentId-based debugging aid.

Acceptance: an extension calling media playback via sendMessage works with a user gesture; uncaught extension-script exceptions appear in AppLog/ExtensionsPanel; prepush green.
design: Gesture propagation is engine-side (mostly free). Our work: surface exceptions via the existing WKWebExtensionController host seams and AppLog; keep per-Space isolation.
acceptance_criteria: Media-playback extension works via sendMessage with gesture; extension-script exceptions visible in log; prepush green
notes: AVAILABILITY VERIFIED 2026-09-15: macOS 26.7 runtime WebKit (build 21624.5) does NOT implement the Safari 27 extension runtime surfaces. objc probe: willSubmitForm absent; WKContentWorld.worldWithConfiguration: absent; getCookiesForURL absent. Extension runtime changes are part of the same WebKit drop — expect none of them on macOS 26.7. Real gate is macOS 27 runtime. The extension-runtime probe caveat in the description stands and is now the whole story.
close_reason: macOS 27.2 runtime has the Safari 27 surfaces: uncaught exceptions and unhandled rejections in extension scripts arrive as WKWebExtensionContext errors (code 7, message with file:line); runtime.getDocumentId is a function in workers. Chord now keeps each extension's distinct script errors with counts (shim lines taken off the worker's line numbers), logs each new one once (extensions category), and shows 'N script errors' with the messages + Copy in Settings > Extensions. Gesture propagation is WebKit's; the shim's sendMessage wrappers call WebKit synchronously so the gesture carries, but no end-to-end media-playback test was written.

title: Native willSubmitForm hook for vault save/update prompts
description:
Safari 27 adds willSubmitForm callback on WKNavigationDelegate + WKFormInfo. Today password-vault form detection is a JS user script (PasswordFormMonitor, ChordEngine) that pierces shadow roots manually and can miss submits. Add a native delegate callback in the Engine that reports HTML form submissions, and route it into the existing vault save/update flow (WebEngine + TabStore). This replaces the fragile JS-driven submission path of ADR 016 and also covers cross-origin and shadow-DOM forms that the script misses.

Native APIs involved: WKNavigationDelegate.willSubmitForm(_:form:completionHandler:), WKFormInfo.

**Availability (verified 2026-09-15):** SDK 27 headers declare it, but macOS 26.7's runtime WebKit (build 21624.5) does NOT implement it — objc runtime probe returns false for the selector. Delegate method is safe to implement now (never fires on 26.7) but feature is dead code until macOS 27 runtime. Gate: . Do not expect it to work on this machine yet.

Acceptance: form submit on a test site triggers the vault save/update prompt even when the form lives inside a closed shadow root; existing PasswordFormMonitor tests stay green; prepush green.
design: RE-POINTED + IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-24 on macOS 27.0 (26A428). The public WKNavigationDelegate.willSubmitForm (macOS 27, Beta) is declared but never invoked — verified with light-DOM, closed-shadow, and trusted-click probes. Working path: the SPI _WKInputDelegate._webView:willSubmitFormValues:frameInfo:sourceFrameInfo:userObject:requestURL:method:submissionHandler: (macOS 26.4+), set via the ObjC-runtime selector _setInputDelegate: (guarded by responds(to:)), the same SPI-by-selector approach already used for geolocation. It fires for a closed-shadow-root form and reports values + sourceFrameInfo + requestURL + method. Extraction by control name via ChordCore/NativeLoginCapture (shares LoginFormClassifier keywords); routed into the existing paneDidSubmitLogin flow. Kept additive: PasswordFormMonitor still covers fetch()-driven SPA logins; the store collapses duplicates.
acceptance_criteria: Submit inside closed shadow root triggers vault save prompt; no regressions in vault fill tests; prepush green
notes: RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-24 on macOS 27.0 (build 26A428): the public WKNavigationDelegate.webView(_:willSubmitForm:) is DECLARED (protocol_getMethodDescription present; Apple docs mark it Beta) but is NEVER INVOKED. Probes with a standalone WKWebView: a light-DOM GET form, a closed-shadow-root form, and a trusted CGEvent button click (form did navigate) all failed to fire it; only didStartProvisionalNavigation/didFinish fired. So the public API is still dead code on 27.0. WORKING PATH: the SPI _WKInputDelegate._webView:willSubmitFormValues:frameInfo:sourceFrameInfo:userObject:submissionHandler: has shipped since macOS 26.4 and reports values + frameInfo + sourceFrameInfo + requestURL + method. Implementing b0s should use that SPI (same 'call the SPI selector by name via the ObjC runtime' approach already used for geolocation), not the public Beta API. Reverted the public-API attempt; no code landed.
close_reason: Implemented via _WKInputDelegate SPI (macOS 26.4+). E2E: closed-shadow-root login triggers the vault save prompt; NativeLoginCaptureTests (9) + LoginCaptureE2ETests (6) green; prepush green.

title: Full-featured Web Inspector (DevTools) for web developers
description:
WKWebView apps get no Inspect menu by default. Enable full Safari Web Inspector via WKPreferences developerExtrasEnabled (private KVC key, technically private API — fine for hobby browser, App Store risk).

Scope:
- Enable developerExtrasEnabled on webview config (per-config, not always-on in release)
- Dev-mode toggle: global vs per-space (decide in design)
- Keyboard shortcut Cmd+Opt+I (Safari convention) via menu item
- Right-click 'Inspect Element' context menu appears automatically from WebKit once flag set
- Inspector is always a detached NSWindow in WKWebView apps (cannot dock like Chrome DevTools)
- Panels: Elements, Console, Sources (debugger/breakpoints), Network, Storage, Responsive Design Mode, Graphics, Performance, Audits

Out of scope / not possible: Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), Puppeteer automation — WKWebView has no public CDP.

User context: works in incognito; useful while testing Netflix DRM/HDR streams.

Right-click on any page shows 'Inspect Element' and opens Web Inspector to that node
Cmd+Opt+I toggles/opens inspector on active webview
Dev-mode toggle exists (decided global vs per-space) and release builds can disable
All standard panels functional: Elements, Console, Sources, Network, Storage, Responsive

title: YouTube page freezes after ad (no scroll, no click)
description:
User report: after an ad is skipped/fast-forwarded on first load, the whole watch page becomes non-interactable once the ad ends — no scroll, no click — until the tab is closed.

Root cause: skipping/rate-blasting an ad triggers YouTube's anti-adblock enforcement wall. YouTubeAdBlocker's CSS only hides the wall's dialog (tp-yt-paper-dialog:has(ytd-enforcement-message-view-model)); the wall is a modal iron-overlay whose open handler pins a full-screen tp-yt-iron-overlay-backdrop (swallows all pointer events) and sets body overflow:hidden (locks scroll). The overlay's close path never runs for a CSS-hidden element, so the page stays frozen after the ad.

Fix (YouTubeAdBlocker.swift): a MutationObserver dismantles the wall — removes ytd-enforcement-message-view-model (climbing to its TP-YT-PAPER-DIALOG host so the overlay stack isn't left with an orphan), removes a visible tp-yt-iron-overlay-backdrop, restores documentElement/body overflow, and best-effort resumes the paused player. Kept the CSS hide as fallback. Added test anchor YouTubeAdBlockerTests.dismantlesEnforcementWall. Verified: swift build -warnings-as-errors clean, full suite 602 tests green.
close_reason: Fixed: YouTubeAdBlocker now dismantles the enforcement wall (removes the iron-overlay backdrop + restores overflow) via MutationObserver instead of only CSS-hiding the dialog. Build clean, 602 tests green.

comments.author: Doddy Rizal Novianto
comments.text: Verified manually (2026-08-14): with the fix in place, skipping/fast-forwarding the pre-roll ad no longer freezes the page — scroll and clicks work after the ad ends. No regression in ad skipping or mute behavior.

title: Fix: YouTube fullscreen video renders black until app is relaunched
description:
User report: sometimes the YouTube player goes fully black in video fullscreen (YouTube's own fullscreen button). Exiting fullscreen (Esc/F) restores the normal page, but re-entering fullscreen is black again, and only quitting Chord fixes it. Reloading the tab does not help.

Root cause: macOS WebKit element-fullscreen reparenting bug (webkit.org/b/313802, reproduced on macOS 26). When a page element goes fullscreen, WKWebView is replaced by a placeholder, moved into a WebKit-owned fullscreen window, then moved back (WKWebView.fullscreenState docs). If the web view is AutoLayout-governed from an ancestor (SwiftUI hosting view), it comes back at a collapsed 0x0 frame and fullscreen video renders black persistently.

Fix (uncommitted, local):
- WebSurfaceContainerView.install: WKWebView now uses frame + autoresizing [.width,.height] instead of Auto Layout constraints (the documented workaround).
- LiveWebView observes WKWebView.fullscreenState; on .notInFullscreen it re-anchors the web view frame to the container bounds and forces a repaint, and logs every transition to the AppLog.

Verification: prepush green (601 tests). Needs a real-app pass: enter/exit YouTube fullscreen repeatedly, especially after the sidebar/pane is resized.
close_reason: User verified manually: black YouTube fullscreen no longer reproduces (2026-08-11). Fix shipped; see ADR 019.

title: Content-blocker weekly refresh is all-or-nothing across both lists
description: ContentBlocker.swift:104-112 concatenates EasyList + EasyPrivacy into one combined string; if either fetch fails the entire refresh aborts and defers to next launch (lastRefresh untouched), so one flaky URL costs both lists for a week. Also hashes/compiles them as one unit, so a change in one list invalidates the other's compiled chunks.
design: Fetch, hash, compile, and store each list under its own identifier (per-list shortHash); track lastRefresh per list; keep the seed fallback and the existing content-hash cache-hit behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A failure fetching EasyList does not lose an already-fetched EasyPrivacy update and vice versa; each list refreshes independently; compiled chunks are keyed per list so a change to one does not invalidate the other's cache
close_reason: ContentBlocker refreshes each list independently (per-list hash identifiers, per-list lastRefresh keys, failed list keeps last good set and retries); seed fallback for never-refreshed slots; legacy single-key migrated read-once; 11 engine tests incl. 3 new per-list; prepush green

title: Crash: QuartzCore assert in new_metal_context after ~7 h of background playback
description: 2026-10-31 04:36:54, Release build at 1d1911e (pid 39202). SIGABRT, __assert_rtn in CA::OGL::new_metal_context <- CA::CG::AccelRenderer::acquire <- CA::CG::Queue::batch_render_callback on a libdispatch worker thread; no Chord frames on the faulting thread. Report: ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Chord-2026-10-31-043654.ips. Context: tab set loaded at 21:50 by an automation script (Space 3: two YouTube tabs; YouTube autoplayed, coreaudiod held PreventUserIdleDisplaySleep for ~7 h, i.e. audio played all night in a background Space); the crash came the moment the script clicked Spaces > Space 3 (Space switch -> remount of parked surfaces). Next: check the other threads in the .ips for what CG/CA drawing was batched (CA::CG accelerated CGContext — a SwiftUI drawingGroup/Canvas or a snapshot/thumbnail render?), check memory/GPU footprint over hours of playback, try to repro: play a video in a background Space for an hour+ then switch Spaces. Unrelated to the 2026-10-28 crashes (EXC_BAD_ACCESS in swift_task_isMainExecutorImpl).
close_reason: Cause in the .ips: thread 14 was FaviconLoader.downsample (NSImage lockFocus off the main thread + NSBitmapImageRep PNG encode) on QuartzCore's accelerated CGContext, whose Metal context creation asserted on the CA::CG queue. Favicons and thumbnails now scale in a CPU CGBitmapContext and encode with ImageIO (ImageDownsampler). Not reproduced (needs ~7 h); the GPU path is gone from Chord's own code.

description: Found while scripting c1k.1: 'open -a Chord <url>' six times created six new Chord windows (SwiftUI WindowGroup opens a scene for each incoming URL), each with a new blank/Google tab, and the URL itself went to the Little Chord panel. title: Minimized window: UI process wakes ~140/s
description: c1k.1 baseline: with the Chord window minimized the UI process (Chord) averaged 140 interrupt wakeups/s; hidden (Cmd-H) 7.5/s; Safari minimized 2.9/s. Something in the UI keeps a timer, display link or animation running while the window is minimized (occlusion handling covers hidden but apparently not minimized; see AppDelegate.attachOcclusionObserver and WebKitEngine.setOccluded). Find it (Instruments Time Profiler / powermetrics --samplers tasks on the UI pid while minimized), stop it while minimized. Accept: minimized UI wakeups <= 10/s; re-run row c.
notes:
2026-10-30: fix committed — occlusion ignores miniaturized windows and also recomputes on didMiniaturize/didDeminiaturize; logs 'occluded: true/false' (app category) on change. NOT yet verified live (display was asleep): minimize the window, expect 'occluded: true' in /usr/bin/log show --predicate 'process == "Chord" AND eventMessage BEGINSWITH "occluded"'; then re-run idle row c (UI wakeups <= 10/s) and close.
2026-10-30 19:23: verified live on Release build at c9ae47f — minimize logs 'occluded: true', restore 'occluded: false', twice. (The command bar panel, when up, correctly keeps Chord visible.) Left: re-measure idle row c (UI wakeups <= 10/s), then close.
2026-10-30 21:03 tab-set run: minimized UI wakeups 148/s with 10 tabs loaded (175 morning; 10.3 with no page). Occlusion now flips (occluded: true logged), but something in the UI still wakes with pages loaded while minimized — and 539/s in front with a paused video. Profile the UI process (Instruments Time Profiler / spindump) minimized with the tab set.
2026-10-30 21:47 FIXED in 1d1911e. Cause: c1k.9 KeepAlivePinger kept a windowless BlankExtensionPage per held worker; each 20 s ping resumed the extension WebContent process, and on re-suspend WebKit's RemoteLayerTreeDrawingAreaProxy::hideContentUntilPendingUpdate waited for a commit a windowless page never makes, so the UI ran a WebKit::DisplayLink (CVDisplayLink thread, ~120 Hz) per such page (pinger + WebKit's own service-worker host page) until the next ping. Diagnosed via sample (7 CVDisplayLink threads, RemoteLayerTreeDisplayLinkClient::displayLinkFired) and /usr/bin/log (hideContentUntilPendingUpdate every ~20 s; wakeup reason WebPageProxy::runJavaScriptInFrameInScriptWorld). Fix: pinger page per ping, released after; controller webViewConfiguration.preferences.inactiveSchedulingPolicy = .throttle. Verified with proc_pid_rusage interrupt wakeups (scratchpad wk.c): UI 4.0/s in front, 4.5/s minimized with a held Bitwarden worker (was 539-1314 / 148). Worker stays in one process, pings every 20 s.
close_reason: UI wakeups 4/s in front and minimized (was 539/148); display-link spin from held workers' windowless pages fixed in 1d1911e

User decision (2026-10-30, from 1mm.6.2): Option A. Extensions stay out of private windows until the user allows each one, as in Chrome/Search.

Allowing/disallowing loads into/unloads from open private Spaces.
