title: Default browser: 'Make Default' in Settings, state check, optional prompt, open .html files
description:
GOAL: Let the user make Chord their default browser from inside Chord, and show whether it already is, the way Safari, Chrome and Arc do. Also let Chord open local .html files.

NO ENTITLEMENT IS NEEDED. On macOS, any app that declares http/https URL types can be the default browser. The "web browser" entitlement (com.apple.developer.web-browser) is iOS/iPadOS only. Passkeys (bead 40q) are a separate entitlement and are still blocked; this task doesn't touch them. Chord ships unsandboxed and Developer ID-signed (see the comment at the top of ChordApp/*.entitlements). Nothing in this task needs the sandbox or a new entitlement.

WHAT ALREADY WORKS (verified 2026-10-29):
- ChordApp/Info.plist declares CFBundleURLTypes with role Viewer and schemes http and https. So Chord already appears in System Settings > Desktop & Dock > Default web browser once LaunchServices has registered it (app in /Applications and launched once).
- ChordApp/AppDelegate.swift ~line 179: `application(_:open urls:)` keeps only the http/https URLs. The first goes to `store.openExternally(url)`, which opens Little Chord or a routed Space (ADR 023). The rest go to `store.openExternallyAlongside`. file:// URLs are DROPPED today.
- There is no call to NSWorkspace setDefaultApplication / urlForApplication anywhere. Check with grep -rn setDefaultApplication ChordApp Packages/Sources.

PART 1: "Default browser" row in Settings > General
- File: Packages/Sources/ChordUI/Settings/GeneralSettings.swift. Add a `defaultBrowserSection` as the FIRST section in the body's list (before `searchEngineSection` ~line 55), following the existing section style.
- It shows either:
  - "Chord is your default browser" with a checkmark, or
  - "Chord is not your default browser" and a "Make Default" button.
- Seam, so it can be tested without changing the Mac's real default:
  - In ChordCore (WebKit-free and AppKit-free): `public protocol DefaultBrowserControlling: AnyObject { var isDefault: Bool { get }; func makeDefault() async throws }`.
  - The real implementation, `WorkspaceDefaultBrowser` in ChordApp or ChordUI (AppKit is allowed there):
    - isDefault: `NSWorkspace.shared.urlForApplication(toOpen: URL(string: "https://example.com")!)`, then compare with Bundle.main.bundleURL by bundle identifier, not by path: a DerivedData build and the /Applications copy have the same id. Check http too, and count as default only if both are Chord.
    - makeDefault: `try await NSWorkspace.shared.setDefaultApplication(at: Bundle.main.bundleURL, toOpenURLsWithScheme: "http")`, then the same for "https" (macOS 12+; Chord's LSMinimumSystemVersion is 15.4, so no #available is needed). macOS shows its own "Do you want to change your default web browser to Chord? Use Chord / Keep Safari" alert. You CANNOT and must not bypass it. If the user picks "Keep", the call throws or the default stays unchanged, so re-read isDefault afterwards rather than trusting the call.
    - Optional, for .html files (Part 3): `setDefaultApplication(at:toOpen: UTType.html)`.
  - Inject it through the environment, the way other services reach Settings (see how SettingsView gets its dependencies), with a fake in ChordTestSupport.
- Refresh: re-read isDefault when the Settings window appears and on NSApplication.didBecomeActiveNotification (the user may have changed it in System Settings while Chord was in the background).
- Wording: plain, no "Pro tip". Match the tone of the other sections.

PART 2: Gentle first-run prompt (optional; follow the user's call on whether it ships enabled)
- At most ONCE, on the 2nd launch or later (never the very first launch, which already has onboarding), when isDefault is false: show a non-modal banner or toast with "Make Chord your default browser?", a [Make Default] button and a [Not now] button.
- Remember "Not now" forever in UserDefaults (key chord.defaultBrowser.prompted) and never nag again. The Settings row stays.
- Use the existing toast mechanism (store.focusedWindow.showToast exists; check whether it supports a button, otherwise use a small banner like the screen-share banner in RootView).
- Never in a private window.

PART 3: Open local HTML files
- Info.plist: add CFBundleDocumentTypes with one entry: CFBundleTypeRole Viewer, LSHandlerRank Alternate (so we don't fight the user's editor for .html), LSItemContentTypes [public.html, public.xhtml]. Optionally also com.apple.webarchive, but only if WKWebView loads it (it does, via loadFileURL).
- AppDelegate.application(_:open:): stop dropping file URLs. For `url.isFileURL` with an html/xhtml/webarchive type, open it in a NEW TAB (not Little Chord: a local file is a document, not a glance) in the focused window's active Space.
- Engine: a file URL has to be loaded with `webView.loadFileURL(url, allowingReadAccessTo: url.deletingLastPathComponent())`, so the page's relative CSS, images and scripts load. Check whether WebKitEngine's load path already handles file URLs (grep loadFileURL Packages/Sources/ChordEngine). If it doesn't, add it at the single place the engine turns a pane URL into a request.
- Session restore of a file tab must work too: the stored URL is file://, so it goes through the same loadFileURL path.
- Security: grant read access ONLY to the file's own directory, never "/" or the home folder. Never for a private Space in a way that persists anything (the tab just isn't saved, as usual).

PITFALLS:
- Stale LaunchServices registrations (old DerivedData builds) can make macOS pick the wrong Chord.app. Developers can run `lsregister -f /Applications/Chord.app` (full path: /System/Library/Frameworks/CoreServices.framework/Frameworks/LaunchServices.framework/Support/lsregister). Mention it in docs/USER_GUIDE.md troubleshooting, not in the UI.
- Don't call setDefaultApplication at launch or without a click. It must always come from a user action.
- Chord's link handling (Little Chord vs routing rules) must not change. This task only makes more links arrive.

TESTS:
- ChordUITests or ChordStoreTests, with a FakeDefaultBrowser:
  - isDefault=false shows the button, and pressing it calls makeDefault once;
  - isDefault=true hides it;
  - a refresh after makeDefault reads the new state.
  View-model level if the UI isn't unit-testable: put the logic in a tiny @Observable DefaultBrowserModel.
- The first-run prompt shows at most once, never on the first launch, never after "Not now" and never in a private window. Use an injected UserDefaults suite.
- File open:
  - a store-level test that opening a file URL makes a new tab with that URL in the active Space;
  - an engine test (real WKWebView) that a file URL whose page references `style.css` beside it loads, and document.styleSheets.length == 1.
- Do not write a test that changes the real system default.

LIVE CHECK (human):
- Build, copy to /Applications, launch, and open Settings > General: it shows "not default".
- Click Make Default: the macOS alert appears. Choose Chord, and the row flips to the checkmark.
- Click a link in Mail or Slack: it opens in Chord (Little Chord).
- Choose Keep Safari instead: the row stays "not default".
- Double-click a .html file, or use Open With > Chord: it opens in a new tab with its CSS.

DOCS: docs/USER_GUIDE.md gets a short "Make Chord your default browser" section (Settings button, or System Settings > Desktop & Dock), plus the lsregister troubleshooting note. README feature list: one line.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] The Settings row shows the real state and the button sets Chord as default through the system alert.
[ ] The state refreshes after a change made outside Chord.
[ ] The optional prompt follows the once-only rules.
[ ] .html files open in a new tab with their relative resources.
[ ] Tests pass, and so does scripts/prepush.sh (it must build against the macOS 26 SDK: these APIs are all macOS 12+, so that's fine).
[ ] One commit, with no Co-Authored-By or other attribution trailer. Docs are updated.

CONTEXT: The repo rules are in AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md and the common context block of epic c1k: build and test commands, one task = one commit, reindex codebase-memory after a commit, don't push unless told. Layering (ADR 011): ChordStore/ChordUI never import WebKit, and ChordCore imports neither AppKit nor WebKit.
notes: Decision (user, 2026-10-29): Settings button only. Do NOT build the Part 2 first-run prompt; skip its tests too.
close_reason: Settings row + Make Default, file .html opening; first-run prompt skipped per user

title: perf.7: Startup — restore extensions after first paint
description:
SYMPTOM: Extension restore runs in the launch path. It is serialized, with a 400 ms sleep after every worker extension, and the worker processes compete with the first restored tab for CPU.

CURRENT CODE (verified 2026-10-29):
- ChordStore/AppEnvironment.swift ~lines 205–213: `store.afterRestore = { await extensionsService.restoreEnabled(spaces: store.spaces); Task { await extensionsService.updateStoreExtensions(in: store.spaces) } }`. TabStore.restore() calls afterRestore at its end.
- ExtensionsService.restoreEnabled (ChordStore/ExtensionsService.swift ~line 187): sorted records → `host.load` → `Task.sleep(400 ms)` when loaded.hasBackgroundContent. The gap is REQUIRED: WebKit fails some workers when several start at the same time. Keep it.
- updateStoreExtensions then checks the Chrome Web Store for updates, which is network work at launch.

PLAN (after c1k.2, which already limits restore to the active Spaces):
1. Delay the restore until the first paint. In WebKitEngine, expose a one-shot `firstPaint` signal (the c1k.1 "perf first-paint" signpost spot: the first didFinish of any pane after launch), for example `public func whenFirstPaint() async`. Surface it to the store through the WebEngine protocol, with a default that returns immediately for fakes.
2. afterRestore becomes: `Task(priority: .utility) { await engine.whenFirstPaint() or a 1.5 s timeout, whichever comes first; await extensionsService.restoreEnabled(...) }`. Use the timeout so a launch with no tabs, or a slow first page, doesn't hold extensions back forever.
3. Move updateStoreExtensions to about 30 s after launch, or to the first idle moment, at .background priority. It's network work plus re-installs, and nothing needs it at launch.
4. Tabs restored before their extension loads: their web views already reference the Space's controller (prepare(space) creates it empty, WebKitExtensionHost.swift ~line 1233). WebKit injects a context's content scripts into existing matching pages when the context loads. VERIFY this for document_start scripts: they may land late, at the context's load time instead of the page's start. For Bitwarden this is fine (it checks the page when it arrives). If a test shows a script missing entirely, reload the tabs that match that extension's host permissions after it loads, but only the ones that haven't been interacted with.
5. Keep the order: the vault reconcile and others that already run at launch stay where they are. Only the extension work moves.

- An extension the user opens in the first second (clicking its toolbar icon) must still work. If its Space isn't loaded yet, the click should trigger ensureLoaded (c1k.2) and then open it.
- The externally_connectable bootstrap source depends on the loaded extensions (WebKitEngine.installExternallyConnectable). It updates on load, and the next navigation picks it up. That's acceptable, but note it in the commit.
- Native messaging hosts (desktop_proxy) start only once Bitwarden's worker connects, which now happens later. Unlocking Bitwarden in the first 2 s after launch may be slower, and that's acceptable.

TESTS:
- ChordStoreTests: with a fake engine whose whenFirstPaint never returns, restore still happens after the timeout (use a short injected timeout in tests).
- With whenFirstPaint returning at once, restore runs, and the fake host's load call order is unchanged.
- updateStoreExtensions is not called during the first N seconds (injectable clock or delay).

MEASURE: c1k.1 `startup` (launch → first paint) median of 5, before and after. Also the time until the first restored tab is interactive: scroll it right away, and record it subjectively.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] Cold start to first paint improves, with the numbers in the commit.
[ ] Extensions are up within about 2 s of the first paint.

title: ExtensionSocket keeps sockets of unloaded extensions open (no orphan sweep)
description:
SYMPTOM (plausible, confirm first)
ExtensionSocket (the WebSocket bridge the worker shim uses, e.g. Bitwarden's SignalR live sync) keeps every Connection in `static var open` until Connection.end runs, which happens only on the port's disconnectHandler, a socket close/error, or a failed open. ExtensionNative documents (stopOrphans) that WebKit does not always call a port's disconnect handler when an extension is unloaded (turned off, removed, reloaded), and sweeps orphaned native hosts on every new connect. ExtensionSocket has no such sweep, so after disabling, removing or reloading an extension its socket can stay connected to the server: the Connection, its URLSessionWebSocketTask (which retains its delegate, the Connection) and the receive loop live on, receiving traffic and dropping it (post() checks port.isDisconnected).

CONFIRM
Temporary Log.extensions.notice in ExtensionSocket.connect and Connection.end with the count of `open`. Enable Bitwarden (logged in, desktop app optional), wait for the socket to open (wss to the Bitwarden notifications host), then disable Bitwarden in Settings > Extensions, and separately reload it. If `open` does not drop, or the socket stays in `lsof -p <Chord pid> -i` / Network inspector, the bug is real.

WHERE
Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/ExtensionSocket.swift (connect, Connection.end, `open`); reference Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/ExtensionNative.swift stopOrphans() and its Live registry; unload path WebKitExtensionHost.unload(slug:in:).

FIX
- Add `static func endOrphans()` to ExtensionSocket: end (tellingPort: false) every Connection whose port.isDisconnected. Call it at the start of connect(_:from:) (as ExtensionNative.connect calls stopOrphans) and from WebKitExtensionHost.unload(slug:in:) after the context is unloaded (also call ExtensionNative.stopOrphans() there for the same reason).
- Optionally key connections by extension origin so unload can end that extension's sockets directly even if WebKit reports the port as still connected.

ACCEPT
- Unit test: a Connection over a port that reports disconnected is ended by endOrphans (if WKWebExtension.MessagePort cannot be faked, extract the sweep decision into a testable function over a protocol, as ExtensionNative.shimWord was in cc13ebf).
- Live confirm step above shows the socket closing on disable/remove/reload.
- If CONFIRM shows WebKit does call the disconnect handler in all three cases on macOS 27.2, close as not reproducible with the evidence.

--------
COMMON CONTEXT (all audit-2026-10-29 tasks)

title: Tab removal paths drift: sweep and delete Space skip tabs.onRemoved and per-pane cleanup
description:
SYMPTOM
Five store paths remove tabs/panes, and each repeats its own cleanup list. They have drifted:

| path | engine.forget | runtimes nil | extensionTabDidClose | cancelSleepTimer | forgetStateResolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| closeTabRemovingEveryPane (TabStore.swift) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| closePane (TabStore+Split.swift) | yes | yes | n/a (tab stays) | no | no |
| sweepNow (TabStore+Sweep.swift) | yes | yes | NO | no | NO |
| deleteSpace (TabStore+Spaces.swift) | yes | yes | NO | no | NO |
| tearDownPrivateSession (TabStore+Private.swift) | yes | yes | yes | yes | NO |

Effects:
- Swept tabs (every 5 min, idle ephemeral tabs) and a deleted Space's tabs never reach WebKitExtensionHost.extensionTabDidClose, so extensions never get tabs.onRemoved for them (password managers, tab managers and ad blockers keep per-tab state keyed on that event), and their ExtensionTabAdapter stays cached in tabAdapters[spaceID][tabID] for the life of the process.
- stateResolution[paneID] and openedPaneIDs (TabStore+Restore.swift forgetStateResolution) leak per pane on sweep, delete Space, private teardown and pane close.
- pendingHistoryURL[paneID] (TabStore.swift, set on URL change, cleared only when a title arrives) is never cleared when a pane closes before its title comes in.
Each is small per tab; the sweep makes it grow steadily over a long session.

WHERE
Packages/Sources/ChordStore/TabStore.swift closeTabRemovingEveryPane (reference: the most complete list), TabStore+Split.swift closePane, TabStore+Sweep.swift sweepNow, TabStore+Spaces.swift deleteSpace, TabStore+Private.swift tearDownPrivateSession, TabStore+Restore.swift forgetStateResolution, TabStore+LittleChord.swift (also removes a pane: check it too).

title: Bitwarden desktop native-messaging port drops every ~10 s
description:
SYMPTOM
Logged 2026-10-28 23:24-23:26 (with the shim's verbose console on): every 10 s Bitwarden's worker logs
  "NativeMessaging port disconnected because of error: unknown"
and reconnects. Each reconnect launches /Applications/Bitwarden.app/Contents/MacOS/desktop_proxy (Mac App Store build 2026.10.0, team LTZ2PFU5D6, sandboxed; its logs in ~/Library/Containers/com.bitwarden.desktop are not readable without Full Disk Access) and redoes Bitwarden's encrypted handshake (setupEncryption). Chrome keeps one port open for as long as the extension runs. Likely the cause of 1mm.12 (slow biometric unlock). Biometric unlock itself works (2026-10-29).

HOW IT WORKS IN CHORD
- runtime.connectNative("com.8bit.bitwarden") -> WKWebExtensionControllerDelegate connectUsing port -> ExtensionNative.connect(_:named:from:) (Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/ExtensionNative.swift). The host manifest is found in the Chrome/Chromium/Edge/Brave/Arc NativeMessagingHosts folders (here ~/Library/Application Support/Chromium/NativeMessagingHosts/com.8bit.bitwarden.json); allowed_origins includes chrome-extension://nngceckbapebfimnlniiiahkandclblb/.
- HostPipe runs the program with Chrome's framing (4-byte length + JSON), `exitGrace` 1.5 s, `killGrace` 2 s, `frameCap` 1 MiB. pipe.onExit -> port.disconnect() (no error text, which Bitwarden reports as "unknown"). port.disconnectHandler -> pipe.stop(). `stopOrphans()` stops hosts whose port isDisconnected and runs on every connect and after every unload.
- ExtensionNative matches Search's (~/perkodingan/Search/Sources/Search/ExtensionNative.swift) apart from formatting and JSON encoding moved into send/request.
- Note that two desktop_proxy processes were running at once (children of Chord) on 2026-10-29 02:13.

STEPS
1. Add temporary logging in HostPipe: launch time, PID, exit status and reason (process.terminationStatus / terminationReason), first 200 bytes of stderr, bytes in and out per message, and who initiated the end (host exit vs port.disconnectHandler vs stopOrphans). Reproduce with Bitwarden unlocked for 2 minutes.
2. Decide which side ends it:
   - Host exits on its own every 10 s -> desktop_proxy is unhappy (e.g. stdin closed early, a framing error, or the desktop app refusing). Check we never close stdin and that framing is little-endian native.
   - Chord stops it -> stopOrphans or a port that WebKit reports isDisconnected while still in use (WebKit MessagePort lifetime; is the WKWebExtension.MessagePort object retained? `Live.keep` holds pipe+port).
   - The extension disconnects -> Bitwarden's NativeMessagingBackground gives up because a reply did not arrive in time; look for timing with the logs.
3. Compare with Search on the same Mac (it uses the same proxy).

ACCEPT
- One desktop_proxy stays up while Bitwarden is unlocked; no disconnect every 10 s over 5 minutes; biometric unlock still works; then re-measure 1mm.12.

---
COMMON CONTEXT (all 1mm.6.x tasks)
- Chord repo: /Users/rizal/perkodingan/webkit-arc-like-browser. Reference browser: ~/perkodingan/Search (Sources/Search/*.swift). Search has ONE WKWebExtensionController for the whole browser; Chord has ONE PER SPACE (WebKitExtensionHost.controllers[space.id], loadedContexts[space.id][slug]). Keep per-Space — every Search step maps to "for this Space's controller".
- Layering (ADR 011): WebKit types stay in Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions; ChordStore (ExtensionsService) and ChordUI see only the WebKit-free ExtensionHost protocol (ExtensionHost.swift). New host methods need a no-op default in the `public extension ExtensionHost` block so test fakes (Tests/ChordStoreTests/ExtensionsServiceTests.swift FakeHost, ExtensionModelTests.swift RecordingExtensionHost) still compile.
- Line numbers below are as of 2026-10-29 and drift; search by symbol name.

title: Bitwarden live sync: SignalR WebSocket handshake fails ('Message is incomplete'), retries ~1/s
description:
SYMPTOM
With Bitwarden unlocked, its worker logs about once a second:
  "Error parsing handshake response: Error: Message is incomplete."
  then "HttpConnection.stopConnection(...) was called while the connection is still in the connecting state."
Bitwarden's live sync (vault changes pushed from the server, SignalR "notifications" hub at notifications.bitwarden.com) never connects, and it retries forever: network traffic, worker wake-ups and log writes every second. Vault changes from other devices only arrive on the next periodic sync.

HOW THE SOCKET WORKS IN CHORD
- A worker's own WebSocket deadlocks in WebKit, so the shim replaces `WebSocket` in workers (ExtensionShimScript.swift ~328-425, class WebSocket extends EventTarget) and carries frames over a native port to ExtensionSocket.swift (URLSessionWebSocketTask). Text frames go as {"text": s}, binary as {"binary": base64}; the shim decodes binary to ArrayBuffer or Blob per `binaryType`.
- ExtensionSocket.swift matches Search's (~/perkodingan/Search/Sources/Search/ExtensionSocket.swift) except comments and formatting. Search's shim WebSocket: ExtensionShims.swift (search "class WebSocket extends EventTarget").

WHAT "Message is incomplete" MEANS
@microsoft/signalr's TextMessageFormat.parse throws it when the received text does not end with the record separator "\u001e". The handshake request is `{"protocol":"messagepack","version":1}\u001e` (text); the server answers `{}\u001e`. Bitwarden uses the MessagePack hub protocol (binary frames after the handshake). So either the separator is lost on the way in or out, the handshake response arrives in a shape SignalR does not expect, or frames are merged/split.

HYPOTHESES TO TEST, IN ORDER
1. The "\u001e" control character is dropped or altered somewhere in: shim send -> native port (JSON) -> ExtensionSocket `task.send(.string)`; or URLSession receive -> ["text": text] -> port -> shim MessageEvent. Log the exact bytes (hex of the first 64 bytes) of the first 3 frames each way in ExtensionSocket (temporary).
2. The handshake response is sent by the server as a BINARY frame (MessagePack transfer format), arrives as ArrayBuffer, and SignalR's parseHandshakeResponse(ArrayBuffer) path fails because the buffer has extra bytes, or the shim's `decode` (atob loop) mangles it. Compare byte length vs the server's.
3. Ordering: the shim's `send` converts binary asynchronously (Promise) but text synchronously, so a binary message queued right after the handshake could overtake it. Check the order on the wire.
4. Subprotocols/headers: SignalR negotiates first over HTTPS (POST /hub/negotiate, then wss://.../hub?id=...&access_token=...). Check the URLSession request carries the same query string, Origin `chrome-extension://<id>` and no unexpected Sec-WebSocket-Protocol.

HOW TO REPRODUCE
- Build and run Chord, unlock Bitwarden, and watch chord.log for "handshake" (it repeats about every second).
- A minimal unit test: a local WebSocket echo server (Network.framework NWListener with NWProtocolWebSocket) plus the shim's worker WebSocket in a real MV3 worker (pattern: ExtensionAdapterTests.windowsCreateOpensTheRequestedTab, which loads a real MV3 background). Send "{}\u001e" both as text and binary; assert the worker receives it unchanged.

FIX AND ACCEPT
- Fix the lossy step; keep ExtensionSocket in step with Search's.
- Acceptance: no "Message is incomplete" in chord.log over 5 minutes with Bitwarden unlocked; a change made in the Bitwarden web vault shows in the extension within seconds; the new unit test passes.

title: prepush: full serial swift test still hangs in ChordStoreTests
description: 2026-10-29: ./scripts/prepush.sh (swift test --no-parallel over all targets) hung 3 of 4 runs inside ChordStoreTests at varying tests (SessionRestoreTests 'Quitting captures every live pane…', TabStore 'Dragging an ephemeral tab into the pinned section…'), with no failure output; a killed run leaves an orphaned swiftpm-testing-helper that hangs later runs. notes:

2026-10-29 sample (ChordStoreTests alone; 2 of 3 runs passed in 1.7 s, run 3 stalled after 'A pane with no stored state still gets a view'): the stalled process has only 2 threads, both idle — main thread parked in CFRunLoopRun (swift_task_asyncMainDrainQueue), one idle workqueue thread, no Chord frames. So no deadlock or spin: an awaited continuation never resumes. Next: run with swift-testing --event-stream-output-path (or .timeLimit traits) to see which test is in flight at the stall; suspects are SessionRestoreTests' settle()/storedState() polling helpers and anything awaiting FakeWebEngine/FakeTabRepository callbacks. title: Bitwarden vault passkeys: windows.create popup must be a real window
description: Bitwarden intercepts navigator.credentials (no Apple entitlement needed for vault passkeys) and opens its passkey UI with chrome.windows.create({type:'popup', url:'popup/index.html#/fido2?...'}) via BrowserPopupUtils.openPopout (forceCloseExistingWindows: true), keeps the returned window id, and closes/aborts the session when windows.onRemoved fires for that id (class FF.connect in background.js: windowClosed$.pipe(filter(id===t)) -> close()+abort(true) -> 'Fido2UserInterfaceSession was closed' -> page gets NotAllowedError). Chord's windows.create (1mm.4, 2026-10-28) turns it into a tab in the Space window and returns that window's id, so the popout has no window of its own. Search (Extensions.swift openNewWindowUsing ~1562, onScreen ~1640) opens a real small window. Port that for type 'popup' so the popout gets its own id and windows.onRemoved fires only when it closes. Also correct 40q: Bitwarden vault passkeys do not need the entitlement.
acceptance_criteria: webauthn.io Register shows Bitwarden's save-passkey screen and succeeds; Authenticate signs in with it.
close_reason: Fixed in 7d37b38; user verified webauthn.io register + authenticate with Bitwarden vault passkey.

title: Re-prepare shim with worker generation on every load
description:
WHY
Chord's shim script carries a worker-generation number the worker uses to tell a fresh background from a restarted one (worker recovery, 899/exn). Chord always stamps 0, so after a revive/reload the worker starts believing it is generation 0 while ExtensionWorkerRecovery says 1+. Search re-prepares the shim with the current generation before EVERY load.

SEARCH REFERENCE
- ExtensionShims.swift:53 `prepare(_ folder:, fresh:, workerGeneration: Int = 0)`: stamp is `version + "-worker-\(workerGeneration)"` (so a generation change re-writes the shim), and `__SEARCH_WORKER_GENERATION__` is replaced with the number.
- Extensions.swift:502-503 in `load(_:)`: `let generation = ExtensionWorkerRecovery.shared.generation(for: item.id)` then `try? await Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) { try ExtensionShims.prepare(folder, workerGeneration: generation) }.value` — off the main thread (Grammarly: 450 ms).
- Shim JS consumer: ExtensionShims.swift:1203 (`const workerGeneration = Number("__SEARCH_WORKER_GENERATION__") || 0`).

CHORD TODAY
- Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/ExtensionShims.swift:32 `prepare(_ folder:, fresh:)`, line ~52 hard-codes `"__SEARCH_WORKER_GENERATION__" -> "0"`; stamp compare is `== version` only.
- Shim JS consumer: ExtensionShimScript.swift:884.
- Generations: ExtensionWorkerRecovery.generation(for: Key(spaceID:, slug:)).
- Load: WebKitExtensionHost.load(_:in:) (~line 290). Prepare also runs from ExtensionInstaller.install/prepareIfNeeded (fresh: true) — those stay generation 0.

STEPS
1. Add `workerGeneration: Int = 0` to ChordExtensions ExtensionShims.prepare; stamp = `version + "-worker-\(workerGeneration)"`; substitute the number. Keep the `ExtensionShims.version` constant itself unchanged (installer's prepareIfNeeded compares the stamp to `ExtensionShims.version` — update that compare to accept any "-worker-N" suffix, e.g. `stamp?.hasPrefix(version + "-worker-")` or split, so a generation bump does not force a full re-unpack from ZIP).
2. In WebKitExtensionHost.load, before `WKWebExtension(resourceBaseURL:)`, when installed.resourceURL is a directory: compute generation for Key(spaceID: space.id, slug: installed.slug) and run prepare off the main actor (Task.detached). Ignore errors (best-effort, like Search's try?).
3. Note: the prepared folder is shared by all Spaces, but generations are per Space. Search has one. Decide and document: simplest is to stamp the max generation across Spaces or accept last-writer-wins; the shim already takes `Math.max(workerGeneration, generation)` from observe replies (ExtensionShimScript.swift:917), so last-writer-wins is safe. Write that in a comment.

PITFALLS
- prepare must not run on the main actor (UI hitch). Swift 6 strict concurrency: ExtensionShims.prepare is static/nonisolated-safe? check, mark `nonisolated` if needed.
- Don't break ExtensionPreparedBundleTests.aStaleShimIsReappliedFromTheStoredZIP (expects stamp == ExtensionShims.version after prepareIfNeeded) — update test expectations deliberately if the stamp format changes.

TESTS
- ExtensionShims test: prepare with workerGeneration 2 writes "2" into chord-shim.js and a stamp ending "-worker-2"; prepare again with 2 is a no-op; with 3 rewrites.
- Installer test still passes (stamp compare accepts suffix).

ACCEPTANCE
- Shim in a loaded extension's prepared folder shows the current generation after a revive (grep chord-shim.js for `Number("N")`).
- Bitwarden still unlocks; probe extensions still load; prepush green.

title: Load-time grants: DNR WithHostAccess, site access, private, identity redirect
description:
WHY
Search grants more at load than Chord. Missing pieces silently break extensions:
- WebKit applies declarativeNetRequest redirect / modifyHeaders rules only with `declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess`; with plain `declarativeNetRequest` it DROPS them without a word (Search: Norma's redirect of a blocked site never happened).
- Identity sign-in tabs: the extension must see its own https://<id>.chromiumapp.org/ address.
- Extensions must never get other extensions' pages or file:// via <all_urls> (WebKit counts chrome-extension:// in <all_urls> once the scheme is registered; Chrome doesn't).

SEARCH REFERENCE (Sources/Search/Extensions.swift)
- load(_:) lines ~516-541: grant all requestedPermissions; .nativeMessaging; `if requestedPermissions.contains(.declarativeNetRequest) { grant .declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess }`; `Extensions.grantSites(context)`; identity pattern `https://\(id).chromiumapp.org/*` when ExtensionShims.allowed(id, context:).contains("identity"); `Extensions.fence(context)`; `context.hasAccessToPrivateData = Extensions.mayGoPrivate(context)`; `context.isInspectable = true`.
- grantSites: line 1174 (uses withheld/reachesExtensions/reachesFiles at 1152-1170).
- fence: line 1194 (deny chrome-extension://*/*, former scheme, webkit-extension://*/*, file:///*, file://*/*; re-grant *://*/* if <all_urls> was granted). MUST be re-applied after any later grant (Search calls it again after permissions.request etc.).
- mayGoPrivate: line 1222 (user setting + manifest "incognito" != "not_allowed").

CHORD TODAY
- WebKitExtensionHost.load (~lines 350-375): reapply persisted grants (permissionsRepository), grant requestedPermissions, grant .nativeMessaging. isInspectable already added (Bitwarden fix). Nothing else.
- Host access in Chord is CONSENT-GATED: ExtensionsService.enable -> host.promptForHostAccess; grants persisted via GrantedPermissionsRepository and reapplied at load. Do NOT port grantSites blindly — Search can auto-grant sites because its install dialog (task 1mm.6.5) was the consent. Until 6.5 lands, keep Chord's prompt for host access; port only the parts that are not host access.
- Private: Chord has private SPACES (space.isPrivate, non-persistent controller), not private tabs.
- Identity: ExtensionAuthWindow.swift handles launchWebAuthFlow; check how it reads the redirect and whether the pattern grant is needed for tabs.query/onUpdated of the sign-in tab.

STEPS
1. DNR: after granting requestedPermissions, if they contain .declarativeNetRequest, grant .declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess. (Rules still limited to granted hosts by WebKit.)
2. Identity: if the manifest requests "identity" (check how Chord's shim lists allowed APIs — ExtensionShims / shim permission list ~ExtensionShimScript.swift:2480), grant MatchPattern "https://<identifier>.chromiumapp.org/*".
3. Port `fence` as a static helper in ChordExtensions; call it at load after all grants, and after every place Chord grants patterns later (grep setPermissionStatus(.grantedExplicitly, for: pattern / requestShimPermissions / setAllHostsAccess / reapply).
4. Private Spaces: decide with the user whether extensions run in private Spaces at all today (check ExtensionsService / enable for isPrivate). If they do, set hasAccessToPrivateData per Search's rule (default off, manifest incognito "not_allowed" refuses). If unclear, leave a note and skip — do not invent a setting UI.
5. grantSites: SKIP until 1mm.6.5 (consent) — note in the commit.

PITFALLS
- fence order matters: WebKit lets an explicit host grant outweigh a broad denial, and a denial covering a grant wipes it — read Search's comments at 1188-1215 carefully.
- Do not grant host patterns without consent (Chord policy, BROWSER_SPEC 7.5c).

TESTS
- Host load test with a fixture manifest requesting declarativeNetRequest: context permission status for .declarativeNetRequestWithHostAccess is granted (use @testable access to loadedContexts as other host tests do).
- fence: after granting <all_urls>, chrome-extension://x/* is denied, file:///* denied, *://*/* granted.
- ExtensionDNRTransformTests still pass.

New host methods need a no-op default in the `public extension ExtensionHost` block so test fakes (Tests/ChordStoreTests/ExtensionsServiceTests.swift FakeHost, ExtensionModelTests.swift RecordingExtensionHost) still compile.

title: Bitwarden popup spins: native-messaging bootstrap rejection
description:
Manual test in ChordTest: Bitwarden installs from the Chrome Web Store (verified CRX3, shim injected) but its toolbar popup never leaves the loading spinner.

Found and fixed while diagnosing (all merged, tests green):
- The shim was not injected into extension HTML pages, only workers/content scripts. It now runs before the popup's own bundles (action.default_popup, options, side_panel, devtools).
- Missing namespaces that Bitwarden touches during startup: chrome.notifications (event streams in a field initializer), chrome.sidePanel, chrome.commands, chrome.management, and chrome.privacy.services.* (it disables Chrome autofill before filling). All defined; privacy.services is per-extension session state because Chord has no Chrome autofill to toggle.
- navigator.userAgent was Safari's; Bitwarden's getDevice() returns null on a Safari UA and its popup/worker call this.device.toString(). Extension contexts now see a Chrome UA (page world untouched).

What still fails (from chord.log via the shim's shim.log channel, background.js):
  console.error: NativeMessaging port disconnected because of error: unknown
  unhandled rejection @background.js
Bitwarden's desktop integration calls chrome.runtime.connectNative('com.8bit.bitwarden') during bootstrap. WebKit surfaces the missing-host failure as a port error that rejects Bitwarden's startup promise; Chrome reports it through runtime.lastError and Bitwarden survives without a desktop app.

Options: (1) make the host path for an unknown manifest behave like Chrome's lastError+disconnect instead of a thrown error; (2) accept as a known incompatibility, like the reference browser's own note about third-party password managers, and point users at Chord's built-in vault. Needs a decision; the popup is otherwise one error from rendering.

Evidence: /tmp/chord-test/bw*.png; ChordTest profile log at ~/Library/Application Support/ChordTest/Logs/chord.log.
close_reason: Fixed. Bitwarden's popup renders and its worker survives startup in ChordTest (screenshot /tmp/chord-test/bw20.png). Causes: shim not injected into extension HTML pages; missing notifications/sidePanel/commands/management/privacy.services namespaces; Safari UA made getDevice() null; connectNative to an unreachable host threw into a rejected promise instead of yielding a port that disconnects like Chrome. Commits 024b776 + 3debdf7; full prepush green.

title: UI smoke suite (XCUITest) for menu, command bar, reader and settings
description:
The 21 epic-899 features have engine/store tests and 16 in-process E2E suites, but nothing drives the real SwiftUI UI. Hand testing needed cliclick + screencapture, which is slow, steals the pointer, and is unreliable for SwiftUI hover/focus (observed: synthetic moves do not drive .onHover; window focus drops between steps).

Add an XCUITest target to Chord.xcodeproj that launches the app with its own data root (CHORD_APP_NAME / CHORD_VAULT_SERVICE already supported) and drives the UI through Accessibility, no cursor.

Minimum cases:
1. Command bar: Cmd+T, type a local URL, Return, assert the page's heading appears.
2. Keyword row: type 'yt cats', assert 'Search YouTube for “cats”' exists.
3. Site chip: type 'red swiftui', assert 'Search Reddit'.
4. Reader: Cmd+Shift+R, assert Reader chrome and reading time; toggle back.
5. Settings search: Cmd+, then Cmd+F, type 'sleep', assert the Sleeping Tabs row.
6. Tab sleep: two tabs, right-click a row, choose Sleep Tab Now, assert the sleeping indicator, click to wake.
7. Blocked pop-up: page opening a pop-up without a gesture, assert the badge and site card row.
8. Address-at-rest: assert a row shows the registrable domain, and that hover reveals the title (this is the case cliclick could not test).

Serve fixtures from an in-test local HTTP server (Network framework) or file URLs — no external network, no user data. Add accessibilityIdentifier only where the AX tree is ambiguous; prefer labels already present.
acceptance_criteria: xcodebuild test -project Chord.xcodeproj -scheme ChordUITests (or equivalent) runs green on a clean machine with the screen unlocked; tests never touch ~/Library/Application Support/Chord or the real vault; a failure names the feature, not a coordinate.
close_reason: Merged. XCUITest target + 9 smoke tests; runs against /tmp/chord-ui-app/ChordUITest.app (bundle id com.rizal.chord.uitest) so data root, prefs domain, WebKit store, Keychain and TCC are the test's own; tearDown asserts the real WebKit store was not modified. 9/9 green via scripts/ui-test.sh.

title: Test suite hangs in full parallel runs
description:
Reported independently by three port agents (.1, .11, .12). Symptoms: a full `swift test` run hangs indefinitely, in different suites each time — ChordStoreTests/SessionRestoreTests around restoreStaysLazy, ChordSecretsTests under an isolated HOME, VaultLockTests, the ChordStore bundle. Every suite passes in isolation and in a split run; .12 got 858 tests green by running '--no-parallel --skip ChordSecretsTests' then the secrets suite alone.

Also seen: a timed-out run leaves an orphaned swiftpm-testing-helper holding the scratch path, and every later run on that path hangs. Killing the orphan fixes it.

Likely three separate issues: (1) keychain/Security access from a test process blocking, (2) an isolated-HOME interaction in ChordSecrets/VaultLock tests, (3) no timeout on the CI gate so a hang looks like 'still running'. Not caused by any port change.

Needed: reproduce deterministically, add per-test timeouts where the wait is unbounded, and make prepush fail fast instead of hanging. Investigate before the merge checkpoint depends on it.
acceptance_criteria: A full parallel `swift test --package-path Packages` completes on a clean machine and in CI, or the offending tests are marked serial with a documented reason; prepush fails within a bounded time instead of hanging; finding recorded in CHECKPOINT.
close_reason: Root cause narrowed: bundles are fine alone and serial (ChordStoreTests 457 tests in 2.7s; full --no-parallel 40s green). Parallel bundle runs block on shared Keychain/preferences state and look like a hang. prepush.sh now runs swift test --no-parallel; two 30-minute hangs gone.

title: Native messaging hosts (Chrome compatibility)
description:
Speak Chrome's native messaging: read host manifests from Chrome's own NativeMessagingHosts folders, check allowed_origins against the calling extension id, spawn the host, and frame messages with Chrome's 4-byte little-endian length prefix over stdin/stdout. The app is unsandboxed, so launching is allowed.

Search reference: Sources/Search/ExtensionNative.swift (16 KB).
design: Process + pipes in ChordExtensions behind ExtensionHost. Watch main-thread blocking: pipe reads must be off the main actor. Depends on the folder install task.
acceptance_criteria: A test host echoes messages both directions; an extension not in allowed_origins is refused; a host that dies closes the port with an error the extension can see; no host is launched without an explicit connect from a loaded extension.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: Install from Chrome Web Store (CRX3 fetch + verify)
description:
Accept a Chrome Web Store link or a bare 32-char a-p extension id, fetch the CRX from the public update endpoint (clients2.google.com/service/update2/crx, acceptformat=crx3, prodversion spoofed to a recent Chrome), verify CRX3, then hand the payload to the folder install pipeline.

Verification: the extension id is the first 16 bytes of SHA-256 of the public key encoded a-p, and the header must carry a matching key plus a signature over the zip. Reject mismatches.

Search reference: Sources/Search/Crx.swift (11 KB).
design: ChordCrypto already has CRX2/CRX3 parsing and RSA verification (ADR 017) — reuse it rather than porting Search's crypto. This task is the fetch + id-derivation + store-URL recognition. Depends on the folder install task.
acceptance_criteria: Installs a real store extension end to end; wrong id, taken-down id and tampered bytes each produce their own error; no unverified byte reaches disk; unit tests over synthetic CRX3 headers (valid, wrong id, bad signature, CRX2 rejected).
notes: Probe (899.2): a real Chrome Web Store extension will still fail on chrome.offscreen until 899.18 lands; keep this blocked behind the shim.
close_reason: Merged to main (c33548e). CRX3 fetch+verify+install path, store UI, 85 extension tests green, branding gate green.

title: Reader mode
description:
Cmd+Shift+R strips a page to its article: prose heuristic (text density, penalise link-heavy blocks) in the isolated world, rendered into a styled sheet with title, byline, images and iframes. Light/dark follows the window. Per-site 'always open in Reader' and an exit that returns to the live page untouched.

Search reference: Sources/Search/Reader.swift (30 KB) + Markdown.swift (renders a site's markdown twin when one exists).
design: Page script + SwiftUI/HTML presentation layer. No WebKit private API. Reuse existing panel/overlay chrome.
acceptance_criteria: Works on a news article, a blog post and a docs page; returns original scroll position on exit; no content from hidden nodes, forms, password fields or other frames; images lazy-load; keyboard accessible.
close_reason: Merged to main (6ab9418); package build + 29 reader/extraction tests green.

title: Import bookmarks from HTML (Netscape format)
description:
File > Import > Bookmarks HTML: parse Netscape bookmark files into the existing folder tree, http(s) only, skip javascript: and data:, keep folder nesting up to a sane depth, report added/skipped counts before committing.

First half of migration; Arc/Chromium imports are separate tasks.

acceptance_criteria: Round-trip test: export ours, import into an empty profile, tree matches; malformed lines skipped not fatal; duplicate URLs land once per folder; counts shown before write.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: Import from Arc (Spaces, pins, favourites)
description:
Read Arc's StorableSidebar.json from a user-chosen Arc data folder and map: Arc spaces -> Chord Spaces, pinned tabs -> Pinned tabs, top-apps -> Favourites. Drop passwords and anything non-http(s). Depth-cap nested folders. Show a dry-run count per Space before importing.

Search reference: Sources/Search/ImportArc.swift (13 KB) + ImportPanel.swift.
design: Pure parser + ChordStore mapping. Mapping (not parsing) is the work: Chord's Space/pin model is richer than Arc's.
acceptance_criteria: Importing a real Arc sidebar produces the same number of Spaces/pins visible in Arc; a re-import does not duplicate; archives are left untouched; corrupt JSON produces a clear error, not a partial write.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: Keyword shortcuts in the command bar (yt cats)
description:
Typing a configured keyword followed by words expands to a %s template: 'yt cats' -> youtube search. Exactly one %s, http(s) templates only, keyword match is case-insensitive on the first token. Offer the match as the top suggestion so Return acts on it.

Also show which keywords exist (a short list in the command bar when the prefix matches a keyword name).

Search reference: Sources/Search/Keyword.swift (3.5 KB).
design: ChordCore pure expansion + ChordUI suggestion source. Storage follows the existing settings pattern; no new file format.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests for expansion, missing %s rejected, two %s rejected, non-http rejected, no keyword collision with the search fallback; visible suggestion row; persisted in settings.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: Address-at-rest: show registrable domain, not page title
description:
When a tab is not hovered/focused, show its registrable domain (eTLD+1) instead of the page title, so a spoofed 'apple.com' title cannot sit next to a real lock icon. Dim the subdomain, ink the registrable domain, show 'Not secure' for http, keep the port for non-default ports.

Requires an eTLD+1 helper and the system public-suffix list. Show punycode when the unicode form could pass for Latin (mixed-script detection).

Search reference: Sources/Search/AtRest.swift, AtRestLine.swift, Registrable.swift.
design: ChordCore: PublicSuffix (vendored list or WebKit API) + eTLD+1 tests. ChordUI: sidebar/nav title rendering. No engine change.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: co.uk, github.io, sub.domain.co.uk, IP literal, localhost, file://, mixed-script punycode; hover/focus crossfades back to the title; http shows the insecure marking; no layout shift.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: Copy Clean Link
description:
Add 'Copy Clean Link' to the page context menu and address field menu, next to the existing Copy URL. Strips known tracking parameters only: utm_*, fbclid, gclid, msclkid, mc_eid, igshid, ref_src, _hsenc. Keeps unknown parameters, their order, encoding and the fragment. Leaves signed URLs alone (X-Amz-Signature, sig, token, expires present) and ignores non-http(s).

Search reference: Sources/Search/CleanLink.swift (4 KB, pure logic).
design: New pure function in ChordCore (no WebKit import). One call site in the existing Copy URL action. No settings.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests over a table of real URLs (tracking only, tracking+legit params, signed URL, no params, non-http, fragment only); menu item copies the stripped URL and shows the existing toast; nothing else about Copy URL changes.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: Site overrides: per-domain CSS, JS and element hiding
description: Users want a site made readable/habitable: hide a rail, kill a webfont, widen a column, drop a sticky header. Add one record per site (pattern, css, js, hiddenSelectors, enabled) — no theme model; theme pickers would be CSS generators if they ever ship. Hiding compiles to a stylesheet (display:none !important), NOT a MutationObserver, because a sheet survives SPA re-render for free and the polling approach is already a standing maintenance item (ADR 013). Ruleset serialized into one WKUserScript built in WebKitEngine.makeContentController(), guarding on location.host, installed only when an enabled override exists. Edits apply on next load with a Reload button (same contract as per-domain UA map). Picker is a top-frame overlay: no cross-origin iframes, no shadow-DOM piercing. Overrides are global, not per-Space. Storage v17_site_overrides.
design: docs/adr/024-site-overrides-are-generated-css.md. New: SiteOverride model + GRDB repository, SiteOverrideCSS (selector list → css), SiteOverrideInjector.makeUserScript(rules:) in ChordEngine, SiteOverridePicker (overlay in-page monitor + message handler, same family as ContextLinkMonitor), Settings → Site overrides editor with CSS/JS text areas + zapper entry point. Migration v17_site_overrides with a fixture from v16. Exclude opaque origins and file:. No import/export in v1.
acceptance_criteria: CSS emitted from selector list hides the element on a TestHTTPServer page; non-matching host installs nothing; no enabled overrides → no user script and no handler; selector shortening prefers id over nth-of-type path; editor applies on save and says Reload; persistence round-trip + v16 fixture migration test; prepush green.
close_reason: Shipped: SiteOverride/SiteOverrides, injector, picker, Settings → Sites, ADR 024, tests. prepush green.

title: Routing rules: host pattern → Space for incoming links
description: Every URL that arrives from outside the current tab lands in a hardcoded place: another app's link goes to Little Chord (AppDelegate.application(_:open:)), cmd-click/target=_blank goes to the active Space (paneRequestedBackgroundTab), window.open becomes a popup (ADR 018). No way to say 'Figma belongs in Design'. Add a rule table host→Space consulted at one choke point, TabStore.spaceForRoutedURL(_:), shared by all three callers. Rules are defaults: split, Peek, private windows and explicit Space switches win. Routed opens go to the target Space in the focused window without switching Space (action toast instead). Host suffix match, longest wins, dot required (no PSL); same matcher as the per-domain UA map. No rules in private windows. Storage v16_route_rules, cascade-delete with Space. Editor in Settings → Spaces. ADR 023.
design: docs/adr/023-routing-rules-decide-the-space.md. New: RouteRule model + RouteRuleStore/GRDB repository, HostPatternMatcher shared with UserAgentOverride (refactor, keep UA tests green). Migration v16_route_rules. TabStore.spaceForRoutedURL consulted from AppDelegate.application(_:open:) before Little Chord, from paneRequestedBackgroundTab, and the popup path. Settings → Spaces section. Cascade delete hooked into Space deletion. No background Space switch; reuse action toast.
acceptance_criteria: Matcher table tests (suffix, longest-wins, TLD rejection); precedence tests (Peek/split/private beat rule); routed cmd-click opens in target Space without changing active Space/selection; rule is inert after its Space is deleted; private windows ignore rules; prepush green.
close_reason: Shipped: RouteRule/RouteRules + settings, routed external + background opens, ADR 023, tests. prepush green.

title: WKContentWorldConfiguration: declarative shadow-root + autofill config for in-page monitors
description:
Safari 27 adds WKContentWorldConfiguration — set content-world properties (autofill scripting, shadow root access, inspectability) at WKContentWorld creation instead of hand-rolled JS.

Chord impact: every in-page monitor manually pierces shadow roots (PasswordFormMonitor.swift:148, LoginFormFiller.swift:58, PictureInPictureMonitor.swift:94) and re-runs on mutation. Declarative shadow-root access would simplify these scripts and strengthen vault form detection. Inspectability config could also simplify developer-mode Web Inspector setup (WebKitEngine developerExtrasEnabled KVC).

Host is macOS 26.7 with Xcode 27 SDK — available now. Evaluate whether the API maps to our per-view WKUserContentController setup on this build.

Acceptance: at least one monitor (prefer PasswordFormMonitor) uses a configured content world with shadow-root access; existing form-detection tests stay green; prepush green.
design: Evaluate WKContentWorldConfiguration on macOS 27 SDK; if it maps to our per-view WKUserContentController setup, adopt for shadow-root piercing and drop manual walks where safe.
acceptance_criteria: PasswordFormMonitor uses configured content world; detection tests green; prepush green
notes:
AVAILABILITY VERIFIED 2026-09-15: macOS 26.7 runtime WebKit (build 21624.5) does NOT implement WKContentWorld.worldWithConfiguration: (objc probe false; pageWorld control probe true, so the probe is sound). SDK 27 declares it; runtime does not. Real gate is macOS 27 runtime.
2026-10-29: this Mac now runs macOS 27.2 (26B123), so re-probe WKContentWorld.worldWithConfiguration:. Note it would not remove the per-mutation full DOM scan in PasswordFormMonitor; that cost is tracked in webkit-arc-like-browser-n97.
close_reason: Committed 12d6c7f. Runtime probe on macOS 27.2 (26B123): worldWithConfiguration: implemented; configured world with allowAccessingClosedShadowRoots sees closed-root inputs, page/plain worlds do not. Adopted for PasswordFormMonitor + handler + LoginFormFiller (shared world; expandos are per world); page world kept below 27. Not a code simplification: shadow walks stay, the gain is closed roots + isolation from the page (setter snooping, forged reports). E2E 50, Engine 78, Core 193, Extensions 112, Store 360 pass.

title: Referrer controls: overrideReferrerForAllRequests + alternateRequest
description:
Safari 27 adds WKWebpagePreferences.overrideReferrerForAllRequests and alternateRequest (modify the main resource request during navigation). Build an Arc-like privacy feature on top: global and per-domain referrer stripping or a custom referrer, applied at navigation time, no JS.

Chord mapping: per-Space config (ADR 011 style) or per-domain rules like the existing UserAgentOverride map (WebKitEngine.setUserAgent, GeneralSettings.perDomainRules). App-level feature, fits the per-Space model.

Host is macOS 26.7 with Xcode 27 SDK — API available now, no macOS 27 required.

Acceptance: per-domain referrer policy (default / strip / custom) applied to main resource + subresources; UI in GeneralSettings; rules persisted via Preferences; tests + prepush green.
design: Extend the UserAgentOverride pattern: ReferrerOverride rule set in Core, consumed in WebKitEngine via WKWebpagePreferences at decidePolicyForNavigationAction time.
acceptance_criteria: Per-domain referrer policy works on main + subresources; UI in GeneralSettings; persisted; prepush green
notes: IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-24 on macOS 27.0 (26A428). API NOTE: the header name is WKWebpagePreferences.overrideReferrer (NOT overrideReferrerForAllRequests); verified functionally that it sets the Referer on the main resource AND subresources (standalone WKWebView probe + E2E). alternateRequest is a separate, broader 'modify the main request' capability and was NOT needed for referrer controls. Implementation: ChordCore/DomainRules.swift (shared host normalise/mostSpecific, now also used by UserAgentRules), ChordCore/ReferrerOverride.swift (ReferrerPolicy default/strip/custom + ReferrerOverride + ReferrerRules.resolve -> nil/''/url), Preferences (prefs.referrerPolicy, prefs.referrerOverrides), TabStore (referrerPolicy + referrerOverrides + set/remove + push at init), WebEngine.setReferrerPolicy seam, WebKitEngine.applyReferrer, NavigationCoordinator migrated to decidePolicyFor:preferences: (applies for every frame before the peek/UA logic), GeneralSettings referrer section (global picker + per-site rules). Tests: ReferrerRulesTests (7), ReferrerStoreTests (3), ReferrerE2ETests (2, subresource referer). prepush GREEN (packages warnings-as-errors + all tests + app build). Not committed (conservative profile).
close_reason: Implemented referrer controls end-to-end; prepush green (packages warnings-as-errors, all tests, app build). Uses WKWebpagePreferences.overrideReferrer on macOS 27 (verified main+subresource). Not committed.

title: ADR 022: Linux port strategy (Swift core + Rust GTK4)
description: Records the accepted Linux port strategy. docs/adr/022-linux-port-swift-core-rust-gtk4.md: shared Swift core + per-platform shells, C ABI boundary, WebKitGTK engine, accepted drops (extensions/PiP/biometric), phased rollout with spike gate, rejected alternatives (CEF, SwiftUI-on-Linux, full rewrite, thin client).

title: P4: Flatpak packaging, CI, release
description: (1) Flatpak manifest on org.gnome.Platform (ships WebKitGTK), .desktop, icon, AppStream metainfo. (2) GitHub Actions: existing macOS pipeline + new Linux (Ubuntu) + Flatpak build pipelines. (3) Flathub publishing (primary); tarball/AppImage as alt. (4) Updater via Flatpak auto-update path. (5) ADR + policy recorded for dropped features and the two-engine maintenance model.
acceptance_criteria: Linux build runs in CI, installs from Flathub, and updates through Flatpak.

title: P3: GTK4 UX parity
description: (1) Command bar + Little Chord via GtkPopover / separate windows (no NSPanel). (2) Split panes, tab drag-reorder, sidebar DnD, tab switcher. (3) Wayland reality: global shortcuts via portal GlobalShortcuts; swipe gestures -> keyboard/gesture alternatives. (4) Adwaita theming, GNOME HIG, dark mode, AT-SPI accessibility. (5) Document as dropped on Linux: extensions, PiP, biometric unlock.

title: P2: WebKitGTK engine parity
description: (1) Space isolation: per-Space WebKitWebContext + WebsiteDataManager. (2) Navigation set: back/forward/reload/stop, zoom, UA, find (with match counts), print (WebKitPrintOperation), devtools, downloads. (3) Content blocking: port seed-blocklist.txt to WebKitUserContentFilterStore compiled JSON. (4) Session state: WebKitViewSessionState <-> interactionState restore. (5) Port JS monitors (media, password form, adblock, geo, screen share) to WebKitUserContentManager message handlers. (6) Permissions: permission-request signal -> xdg-desktop-portal (camera/geo/screen) + D-Bus org.freedesktop.Notifications. (7) Secrets: libsecret vault backend (no biometric). (8) DRM: Widevine Flatpak extension (GStreamer).
acceptance_criteria: Parity with the macOS engine across the mapped WebEngine capabilities, verified on a real Linux desktop.

title: Linux port: Swift core + Rust GTK4 shell
description: Make Chord a real native browser on Linux while keeping the macOS app untouched. Strategy fixed by ADR 022: shared Swift core (ChordCore/ChordPersistence/ChordStore) + per-platform shells. macOS shell stays today's WebKit/SwiftUI code (moved into ChordEngineApple/ChordUIApple). Linux shell is new: Rust + GTK4 + libadwaita + WebKitGTK (webkitgtk-6.0). Core<->shell boundary is a C ABI (chord_c.h). Accepted drops on Linux: extensions, PiP, biometric unlock; DRM = Widevine. See docs/adr/022-linux-port-swift-core-rust-gtk4.md
design: Phases: P0 carve seam (no behaviour change, macOS stays green), P1 spike (decision gate: prove Swift staticlib + bindgen + Rust GTK4 + threading bridge), P2 engine parity, P3 UX parity, P4 Flatpak packaging + CI + release.
acceptance_criteria: Chord builds, runs, and passes existing tests on macOS from main with the seam carved. Linux shell builds via SwiftPM + Cargo, loads a URL, round-trips state through the core. Flatpak package published to Flathub.

title: App-driven Picture-in-Picture (View menu, Cmd+Ctrl+P)
description: Float the active page's video into a native macOS PiP window via the legacy webkitSetPresentationMode path, with the private WKPreferences allowsPictureInPictureMediaPlayback KVC flag. Includes a mode-flip verification, an event-only watcher for label correctness, and E2E coverage.
close_reason: Released in 1.10.0

title: Global hotkey: toggle Meet mic from any window
description:
During a share, the Meet tab lives in a window/panel you are not focused on; toggling mute requires switching back. Fix: a global hotkey (default Cmd+Shift+M, configurable) toggles Meet's mic without leaving the shared tab.

Feasibility: Meet exposes no public JS API. Meet's native mute shortcut is Cmd+D (macOS). Deliver it as a real key event to the Meet tab's WKWebView: make the Meet window key (it must be key-capable — the compact panel from webkit-arc-like-browser-xku is), focus the webview, then post Cmd+D via CGEvent. The page's own shortcut handler does the rest — no DOM scraping, robust to Meet UI changes. Fallback: if Cmd+D stops mapping, click the mic button via injected JS (selectors change often; last resort).

Design: a Meet control bridge user script (pattern: ScreenShareMonitor.swift — injected at documentStart, reports call state to the store via window.webkit.messageHandlers) tracks which tab is 'in a Meet call'. Hotkey handler asks the store for the most-recent Meet tab, makes its window key, and sends the key. If the panel is not built yet, the hotkey still works on any Meet tab in any window.
design: See description. Key-event delivery (Cmd+D) over DOM scraping. A user script (ScreenShareMonitor pattern) reports meet call presence; store routes the hotkey to the most recent Meet pane.
acceptance_criteria: 1. With a Meet call running in one window and another window focused, pressing the hotkey toggles mute/unmute; focus stays where it was (no visible window switch). 2. Works on Meet tabs in both normal windows and the compact panel. 3. Hotkey is configurable and shown in the command palette / menu. 4. No dependency on Meet DOM selectors for the primary path.
close_reason: Shipped: Toggle Meet Mic Cmd+Shift+M via DOM click (no focus switch), companion-first routing, tested.

comments.author: Doddy Rizal Novianto
comments.text: SHIPPED (2026-09-02). Implementation note — the primary path pivoted from Meet's Cmd+D shortcut (key delivery) to a DOM click on the mic button (MeetMicController.toggleScript). Reason: delivering Cmd+D requires the Meet window to become key, a visible focus switch that violates acceptance #1 (focus stays where it was). evaluateJavaScript runs on a background webview, so the DOM click toggles mic with zero focus change. Accepted trade-off: Meet DOM selectors drift; the aria-label 'microphone' match is the documented upkeep risk (mirrors YouTubeAdBlocker). Shortcut is fixed Cmd+Shift+M (menu item in the tab command group) — 'configurable' is deferred to a future preferences item. title: Meet companion: compact floating panel for sharing-time controls
description:
Problem: to share an exact tab from Google Meet, the shared tab must be full-bleed in its own window, and Meet must live in another window. Toggling mic/cam forces tab-switching back to Meet.

Goal: a compact, always-on-top 'Meet companion' panel — Meet runs in it, the shared tab stays fullscreen in the main window, and Meet's controls stay visible at all times without covering the shared content.

Feasibility (verified): capture is window-based, not tab-region. getDisplayMedia is NOT intercepted (no public WKWebView hook, NavigationCoordinator.swift:392-395) — it falls to the native OS picker, so 'share exact tab' = share a window holding one tab. A floating NSPanel is a separate surface, so ScreenCaptureKit window capture never includes it. Reuse the existing LittleChordPanel pattern (LittleChordPanel.swift:49: .floating level, borderless, resizable, .moveToActiveSpace).

Design: like LittleChordPanel but for the current tab — a 'Demote to compact panel' action (tab context menu / command) pulls the active tab into a small always-on-top NSPanel while keeping the tab alive in the store (pattern: TabStore+LittleChord.swift keeps a pane out of [3gH        H        H        H        H        H        H        H        H        H        H). Promote back to a full tab to return. The panel is a normal key-capable window so Meet works fully inside it (unlike .nonactivatingPanel used by LittleChord, which is for links from other apps).
design: See description. Build on LittleChordPanel (borderless, .floating, .fullScreenAuxiliary, .moveToActiveSpace) but key-capable (canBecomeKey = true) so Meet works inside it. Store-level demote/promote keeps the pane alive off the tab list (TabStore+LittleChord.swift pattern). Caveat: works only when sharing a window/tab, NOT whole-screen — screen sharing captures the overlay.
acceptance_criteria: 1. From any tab, 'Demote to compact panel' moves it into a small floating always-on-top window. 2. Meet running in the panel can start a Google Meet call and present a window (the main window's fullscreen shared tab). 3. During the share, the compact panel is NOT visible in the captured output (verify: panel floats over the shared window, capture shows only the shared tab). 4. 'Promote to tab' returns the panel back into the main window as a regular tab, preserving the live page (no reload). 5. Panel position/size persist across sessions.
close_reason: Shipped: compact floating panel (demote/promote/discard + persistence), commands + context menu, 11 CompanionTests green, prepush green.

title: Command bar: autocomplete misses www.-forced domains
description: Inline domain autocomplete (webkit-arc-like-browser-354) collects raw url.host() strings. Google/YouTube redirect to a 'www.' host, so history holds 'www.google.com' and typing 'you'/'goog' never prefix-matches 'www.youtube.com'/'www.google.com'. GitHub/SO don't use www, so they worked. Fix: strip a leading 'www.' when collecting autocomplete domains.
design: autocompleteDomain(of:) helper: host minus leading 'www.', deduped via the existing Set. Regression test: 'goog' -> google.com.
close_reason: Stripped leading 'www.' when collecting autocomplete domains (autocompleteDomain helper); regression test for 'goog' -> google.com. 715 tests green.

title: Command bar: inline domain autocomplete
description: QoL #1. Chrome-omnibox-style prefix completion: type 'you', the bar suggests 'youtube.com' with the suffix highlighted; Enter confirms. Currently the ranker only fuzzy-matches STORED urls/titles (CommandBarRanking.swift) and never EXTENDS a typed prefix into a known domain; URLInput only navigates complete lookalike hosts. Sources: history domains + open-tab domains (no network). Needs its own design: where the completion text lives in CommandBarView, arrow-key semantics while a suffix is highlighted, dedupe against the existing navigate row. The named follow-up in docs/design/command-bar-search-prefix-and-top-sites.md.
design: DESIGN (2026-08-28): Chrome-style inline domain completion. ChordCore: Suggestion gains an optional 'completion: String?' (untyped suffix, default nil). New autocomplete source in CommandBarRanking: on a non-empty, space/slash-free query, collect known dot-domains from history hosts + open-tab hosts (no network), pick the lexicographically-first that the trimmed lowercased query is a strict prefix of, and emit one .navigate(url: https://domain) row with completion = leftover suffix. Scored completionBias(500) so it ranks just below the fallback. Dedupe vs navigate: fully-typed domains (suffix empty) never match, so resolve/navigate fallback owns them. UI (CommandBarView/CommandBarRow): when completion != nil, title renders as prefix + dimmed suffix. Arrow keys move row highlight normally (no special state); selecting the autocomplete row and pressing Return navigates to the completed URL. Typing past the prefix naturally clears it (prefix no longer matches). Accepts: prefix -> domain+highlighted suffix; Return on it navigates; divergence clears.
acceptance_criteria: Typing a prefix of a known domain (from history or open tabs) shows the domain with the untyped suffix highlighted; Enter navigates to the completed domain; typing diverges from the suggestion clears it.
close_reason: Added Suggestion.completion + autocomplete source (history/open-tab domains, completionBias 500); CommandBarRow dims the untyped suffix; Return navigates to completed URL. Tests green (705).

title: Command bar: top sites on empty query
description: QoL #2. Opening the bar with an empty query currently shows only open tabs (history/archived/commands/fallback all guard query.isEmpty in CommandBarRanking.swift). Add a topSites(input:limit:6) source, active only on empty query, scoring cachedHistory (already per-Space, already loaded) with the exact history formula (min(visitCount*3, visitCountMax) + recencyBonus). Rows are .history so activate()/UI untouched. Private windows lose it for free (store passes history: []). Spec: docs/design/command-bar-search-prefix-and-top-sites.md.
acceptance_criteria: Empty query shows top sites below open tabs, ordered by visit count, bounded at 6; empty history -> no rows; private window -> none; existing RankingTests pass.
close_reason: Added topSites source (history formula, base 0, limit 6) active only on empty query; factored shared historySuggestion builder. Tests green (699).

title: User-Agent freshness audit (track Safari version)
description:
Netflix and other DRM providers negotiate stream quality (resolution/bitrate/HDR) based on the User-Agent and capability signals the browser sends. WKWebView UA is derived from Safari; when Safari upgrades, the UA string in Chord may fall behind, causing services to downgrade or refuse streams.

Scope:
- Audit current WKWebView UA vs latest Safari version on this macOS
- Determine how UA is produced (default WKWebView UA vs custom override in Chord)
- Add a check/alert or scheduled maintenance item to bump UA on Safari/macOS updates
- Document expected UA format and where it lives in the codebase

Relation: WebKit upgrade workflow is covered by chord-browser-maintenance; this is the UA-specific slice.
design: Grep codebase for customUserAgent / UA overrides. Compare default WKWebView UA (WebKit version baked by SDK) vs Safari shipping UA. Document in maintenance skill or ticket. Only override if a real downgrade is observed.
acceptance_criteria:
Current UA in Chord identified and compared against latest Safari UA for this macOS
Gap detection method documented (manual or automated)
UA location in codebase documented with bump procedure
DRM stream quality negotiation verified not downgraded by stale UA
close_reason: Audit: macOS/Safari 26.6.2; bumped safariVersionToken 26.5->26.6. Documented single-source-of-truth + bump procedure in maintenance skill.

title: DRM capability diagnostics panel
description:
Netflix removed its secret menus (debug overlay + netflix.com/testpatterns) in 2023. Add an in-app diagnostics panel for the Chord browser that reports DRM/streaming capability truth directly from the engine.

Runs navigator.mediaCapabilities.decodingInfo against the profiles Netflix actually uses:
- video/mp4 hvc1 (HEVC/HDR10) 4K
- dvhe / dvh1 (Dolby Vision)
- audio/mp4 ac-3 (5.1), eac-3 (5.1/7.1), mp4a.40.2 (AAC)
Also surface: playback error codes from webview (Netflix 2003 etc), HDCP chain warnings (DisplayLink docks / non-HDCP adapters silently cap to 720p).

Motivation: dev wants to distinguish 'browser can't do it' from 'Netflix won't serve it'. FairPlay movie playback already works (webkit-arc-like-browser-das context); this is verification tooling.

Consider extending to a hidden Dev menu (consistent with Web Inspector dev-mode work).
design: Reuse a hidden WKWebView or evaluateJavaScript on current webview to call navigator.mediaCapabilities.decodingInfo for a fixed profile matrix. Render results in an in-app window/panel. Hook webview media error events for error-code capture. Place behind Dev menu toggle consistent with webkit-arc-like-browser-das.
acceptance_criteria:
Panel shows per-codec supported/not with full capability details (HEVC, DV, AC-3, E-AC-3, AAC)
Panel shows playback error codes when DRM playback fails
HDCP/display-chain warning surfaced when applicable
Accessible without Netflix secret menus (own UI)
close_reason: DRM Diagnostics panel (Develop > DRM Diagnostics, Cmd+Opt+D): Netflix profile matrix (HEVC 4K HDR, DV dvhe/dvh1, AC-3, E-AC-3, AAC), HDCP display-chain probe, live media/EME error capture via DRMDiagnosticsMonitor.

title: Page zoom shortcuts (Cmd+-, Cmd++, Cmd+0)
description:
Standard browser keyboard shortcuts missing in Chord:
- Cmd+- : zoom out
- Cmd++ : zoom in
- Cmd+0 : reset to 100%
Full-page zoom (not text-only), same behavior as Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Edge.

WKWebView support: macOS 10.13+ webview has pageZoom (WKWebView.pageZoom) and magnification. Evaluate which to use:
- pageZoom: full-page zoom on the webview layer (0..1 scale)
- magnification: similar

Considerations:
- zoom level persistence per-space or global (decide in design, consistent with Web Inspector dev-mode ticket)
- show current zoom in UI? (e.g. status bar / menu tick) — optional
- touchpad pinch zoom behavior already native in WKWebView, unaffected
design: Wire Cmd+-, Cmd++, Cmd+0 as menu items with key equivalents (standard on macOS). Apply via WKWebView.pageZoom. Decide persistence model consistent with the Web Inspector dev-mode ticket (webkit-arc-like-browser-das). Verify against other Chromium-family behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
Cmd+- zooms out, Cmd++ zooms in, Cmd+0 resets to 100%
Zoom is full-page (layout/viewport level), not just font size
Zoom state persists per decision (global vs per-space)
Shortcuts work in incognito/private tabs too
close_reason: View menu: Zoom In Cmd+=, Zoom Out Cmd+-, Actual Size Cmd+0 via WKWebView.pageZoom, global persistence in Preferences, PageZoom ladder + store/engine tests.

title: Support web geolocation (Google/Apple Maps) via WKUIDelegate + CoreLocation
description:
Add navigator.geolocation support so Google Maps / Apple Maps web can request location.

Three layers, mirroring the existing camera/mic pattern:

1. Engine (permission gate)
- Add webView(_:requestGeolocationPermissionFor:initiatedByFrame:decisionHandler:) to the WKUIDelegate extension in Packages/Sources/ChordEngine/NavigationCoordinator.swift (~line 273), alongside requestMediaCapturePermissionFor.
- Add .geolocation to SitePermissionKind (Packages/Sources/ChordCore/SitePermission.swift).
- Add paneRequestedGeolocation to WebEngineDelegate protocol (Packages/Sources/ChordEngine/WebEngine.swift), reuse requestSitePermission per-origin ask-once + persistence.

2. App (OS consent / TCC)
- Info.plist: NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription.
- Request CLLocationManager.requestWhenInUseAuthorization() at launch in AppDelegate so the app appears in System Settings > Privacy > Location Services.
- Link CoreLocation.
- No sandbox entitlement needed (app is unsandboxed, same tradeoff as camera/mic in Chord.entitlements).

3. Caveat
- macOS WKWebView geolocation historically unreliable (WebKit bug 140208). The delegate was only promoted from private SPI to public API in Feb 2026 (WebKit PR #58447), so requires a recent SDK. Test early on maps.apple.com and google.com/maps. Fallback if WebKit won't deliver coordinates: intercept navigator.geolocation via a shim like NotificationBridge, serving position from the host CLLocationManager (the Electron-on-macOS approach).
design: Wire the new WKUIDelegate geolocation method into NavigationCoordinator, add SitePermissionKind.geolocation, extend WebEngineDelegate/TabStore exactly like paneRequestedMediaCapture. App layer: CLLocationManager auth request at launch + Info.plist usage string. Verify WebKit actually delivers position on macOS before committing; otherwise implement a navigator.geolocation shim bridging the host CLLocationManager.
acceptance_criteria: Site asks for location, user sees one per-origin prompt (first time), then remembered decision. maps.apple.com and google.com/maps resolve coordinates when granted. Denying per-origin blocks that site only. Works across Spaces (decision scoped per Space).
close_reason: Working: Google Maps geolocation confirmed in the field — per-origin prompt, OS TCC prompt, coordinates delivered via the navigator.geolocation shim + host CLLocationManager. Prepush green (638 tests, app builds).

title: User-Agent version tokens are stale and internally inconsistent
description: WebKitEngine.swift:370 hard-codes 'Version/26.5 Safari/605.1.15' as the live UA suffix, while UserAgent.swift:34 prefills the Settings custom field with Version/17.5 (defaultTemplate) and the presets carry 17.5/126/127 too. The app advertises two different Safari versions, and the token is hard-coded so it drifts from the actual WebKit engine version over time. UA-vs-engine feature mismatch is itself a fingerprint signal.
design: Centralize the Safari version token in one constant (e.g. in BrowserCore next to UserAgent.swift) and have WebKitEngine.swift:370 + UserAgent.swift:34 reference it. Match the token to the SDK's shipped WebKit version.

title: YouTube ad sometimes not skipped or fast-forwarded
description: YouTubeAdBlocker tick() fails intermittently: an ad plays to the end instead of being skipped/fast-forwarded. Suspected causes in Packages/Sources/BrowserEngine/YouTubeAdBlocker.swift: (1) once-only playbackRate bump that YouTube's player resets to 1x, (2) skip-button click returns early and swallows the fallback seek/blast when the button is disabled/custom, (3) targets only the first <video> while YouTube A/B-tests ads on a separate element and the watch page has an ambient background video.
