title: A refused redirect to an extension page leaves the tab silently blank
description: NavigationCoordinator: when a main-frame navigation goes to an extension page (needsNewView) and engine.mayOpen(url, from: site) refuses it (e.g. source is a new tab's about:blank, so site is nil), the policy cancels and nothing else happens: the tab stays an empty document with no explanation. Found via e3x (uBOL strictblock redirect from a new tab). Options: load the original URL instead, show an error page naming the extension, or allow DNR redirects (navigationType -1 / other) from about:blank when the original request was user-initiated. Low priority now that the uBOL trigger is fixed (shim leaves out regex+requestDomains redirects).
close_reason: A main-frame navigation to an extension page that mayOpen refuses now shows a short page naming the extension and the address (Chrome's ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT spot) instead of leaving the old/empty document.

title: Recording pill while an extension records the screen
description: Since 1mm.4's desktopCapture bridge (ExtensionCapture, chordCapture channel), Loom and Awesome Screenshot can record via the shim-held getDisplayMedia, but Chord shows no indicator that a recording is running. Search has RecordingIndicator.swift (~/perkodingan/Search): a pill naming the extension, with Stop. Port it: the host knows when ExtensionCapture.record hands out a stream (track ended = stop); expose that WebKit-free through ExtensionHost (no-op default), show the pill in the Space window (ChordUI), Stop ends the tracks via callAsyncJavaScript in the recording page. Accept: recording with Loom shows the pill with the extension name; Stop ends the recording; the pill goes when the extension stops on its own. Tests: host state on record/stop with a fake page.

Tests: fake recording page start/stop/purge, store Stop. Not tried with real Loom.

title: perf.8: Perf budget in prepush/CI so regressions fail
description:
WHY: Without automated budgets, every new feature adds back a script or a timer, and the gains from c1k.2–7 wear away.

WHAT: Add cheap, deterministic perf checks as normal tests that run in scripts/prepush.sh, plus a heavier opt-in check.

1. Static budgets. These are plain unit tests in ChordEngineTests and ChordExtensionsTests, fast and not flaky:
   a) User-script count and size: build a WebKitEngine with default settings (developer mode off, no overrides, no extensions), read the configuration's `userContentController.userScripts`, and assert that count ≤ BUDGET_SCRIPTS and the sum of source.utf8.count ≤ BUDGET_BYTES. Assert separately how many have forMainFrameOnly == false.
   b) No forever timers in the shim: assert that the ExtensionShimScript source has no `setInterval(` except an allow-list of reviewed ones, each listed with the reason. Do the same for each ChordEngine page script.
   c) Popup sizing: an ExtensionPopup test (from c1k.5) asserts that the timer is nil 3 s after the last change.
2. Runtime budget. This is a real WKWebView test and a bit slower, but stable:
   d) Load about:blank, plus a plain https test page from the in-process test server LoginFillE2ETests uses, in a WKWebView configured like a real tab. Wrap setInterval/setTimeout before Chord's scripts run, with a document-start script added FIRST, and count live intervals after 2 s. Assert ≤ BUDGET_INTERVALS_PLAIN (likely 0). Do the same on a youtube.com-based-URL page (loadHTMLString with baseURL youtube.com, as YouTubeAdBlockerTests does) and assert ≤ 1 (the 2 s safety tick from c1k.5).
3. Opt-in heavy check: `CHORD_PERF=1 scripts/prepush.sh` also runs `scripts/perf-baseline.sh startup` and fails if the median exceeds docs/perf/BUDGETS.md's startup budget × 1.15. It isn't the default, because launch timing is noisy on shared machines. This follows the CHORD_REAL_EXTENSIONS pattern already in prepush.sh.
4. docs/perf/BUDGETS.md: each budget, its current value, why, and how to raise it ("change the constant in the test AND justify it in the commit").
5. CI: the static and runtime tests run wherever `swift test` runs (prepush and the release workflow on macos-26), so no workflow change is needed. Confirm that the tests compile against the macOS 26 SDK: no 27-only API.

PITFALLS:
- Put the budget numbers in ONE place (a `PerfBudget` enum in ChordTestSupport) so changing them is deliberate and easy to review.
- Set the budgets AFTER c1k.3 and c1k.5 land, at those new values, not today's.

ACCEPTANCE:
[ ] Adding a dummy always-on user script, or a `setInterval(f, 1000)` in the shim, makes `swift test` fail with a message that names the budget and BUDGETS.md. Show it locally, then revert the dummy.
[ ] BUDGETS.md is committed.
[ ] prepush passes. CHORD_PERF=1 works on a dev Mac.

================ COMMON CONTEXT (same on every c1k.* task) ================
GOAL: Chord is a SwiftUI and AppKit browser on WebKit, the same engine as Safari. Raw page speed is therefore WebKit's. What Chord can win or lose is everything it adds on top: user scripts, extension controllers and workers, timers, SwiftUI redraws, and web views it keeps alive. The target is "no worse than Safari on the same tab set". Each task removes one of those added costs.

REPO MAP:
- Packages/Sources/ChordEngine: WebKit wrapper (WebKitEngine, WebViewPool, LiveWebView, the page user scripts *Monitor/*Bridge/*Controller).
- Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions: WKWebExtension host (WebKitExtensionHost, ExtensionShimScript = JS shim injected into every extension, ExtensionNative, ExtensionPopup).
- Packages/Sources/ChordStore: app state (TabStore, PaneRuntime, WindowState, ExtensionsService, AppEnvironment).
- Packages/Sources/ChordUI: SwiftUI views (RootView, Sidebar/*, Content/*, Toolbar/*).
- ChordApp/: the app target. Chord.xcodeproj builds it.
- Layering (ADR 011): ChordStore and ChordUI never import WebKit. They talk to extensions only through the `ExtensionHost` protocol (Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions/ExtensionHost.swift). Every new protocol method needs a no-op default in the `public extension ExtensionHost` block (~line 160), so fakes and tests keep compiling.

BUILD / TEST / GATE:
- Build packages: `swift build --package-path Packages -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`. Warnings are errors.
- One test target: `/usr/bin/timeout 600 swift test --package-path Packages --filter ChordEngineTests --no-parallel`. Run one target at a time, and run `pkill -f swiftpm-testing-helper` between runs: ChordStoreTests sometimes hangs (bead x4b), so retry once before you suspect your change.
- The full gate before any commit is `scripts/prepush.sh`: package build, all tests, then the xcodebuild app build.
- Run the app: build the Chord scheme in Debug (`xcodebuild -project Chord.xcodeproj -scheme Chord -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build`) and open the .app from DerivedData.

LOGGING / MEASURING:
- Use `Log.<category>.notice("...")`, with the categories in ChordCore's AppLog. NSLog does NOT reach the unified log on this setup. AppLog has no `privacy:` argument.
- Read logs with `/usr/bin/log show --last 5m --predicate 'subsystem BEGINSWITH "app.chord"' --info`. Use the full path, because `log` is a shell function in the dev shell, and use `log show` because `log stream` exits early.
- Energy: `sudo powermetrics --samplers tasks,cpu_power -i 5000 -n 12` (it needs a human for sudo), Activity Monitor > Energy, Instruments (Time Profiler, SwiftUI, Energy Log, os_signpost).
- Every task records BEFORE and AFTER numbers with the c1k.1 harness (scripts/perf-baseline.sh once it exists) and puts them in the commit message.

RELEASE CONSTRAINT: Release CI builds against the macOS 26 SDK, while dev Macs have Xcode 27. `#available` only guards at run time, so any API that exists only in the macOS 27 SDK must be reached by name (NSClassFromString / KVC / perform). See `bd memories macos26` and PasswordFormMonitor.closedRootsWorld.

WORKFLOW RULES:
- `bd update <id> --claim` before you start.
- One task = one commit, which includes its tests. Message style: `Area: what changed, in plain words` (see git log). No Co-Authored-By or other attribution trailer.
- Don't push unless told to.
- After a commit, reindex codebase-memory (index_repository, mode full).
- `bd close <id>` with a short reason quoting the before and after numbers.
- If you find more work, file a new bead under epic c1k instead of widening the commit.
close_reason: PerfBudget (ChordTestSupport) + tests: 3 user scripts / 1 every-frame / 45,000 bytes (42,461 now), reviewed setIntervals only (YouTube 2, Geolocation 1, shim 0), live intervals 2 s after load 0 plain / 1 YouTube; docs/perf/BUDGETS.md; CHORD_PERF=1 prepush checks startup <= 2545 ms (not run today, user away). Over-budget failure shown locally with the byte budget.

title: LiveWebView.tearDown cancels its own about:blank load and removes only some handlers
description:
SYMPTOM
LiveWebView.tearDown() (Packages/Sources/ChordEngine/WebViewPool.swift), run on every eviction:
1. Calls webView.load(about:blank) to "destroy the active document context", then at the end calls webView.stopLoading(), which cancels that provisional navigation. The page document is therefore never replaced by teardown; it only goes when the WKWebView deallocates. If anything still holds the view (a pending evaluateJavaScript, a popup's opener chain, an extension), the old page keeps running (timers, audio already paused by the JS step, network).
   Note TabStore+Split.swift closePane relies on teardown navigating to about:blank ("whose KVO snapshot would otherwise overwrite this pane's URL") — check that reasoning still holds whichever way this is fixed.
2. Removes only some script message handlers by name: Media, ContextLink, ContextImage, ScreenShare, PasswordForm (its world), PictureInPicture, DRM. makeContentController (WebKitEngine.swift) also adds SiteOverridePicker, NotificationBridge.show, the with-reply NotificationBridge.permission and GeolocationBridge handlers, ChromeStoreRelayHandler (storeRelay), and the extension host's worker-recovery and capture handlers (ExtensionWorkerRecovery.swift, ExtensionCapture.swift). Today this is not a cycle (each view has its own controller and the handlers do not retain the view), so impact is low, but the list is a maintenance trap: every new handler must be remembered here.
3. Leftover generated comments ("// 3. Your existing retain-cycle cleanup", "// 1. Force WebKit's media daemon to stop immediately") that do not match the file's comment style.

FIX
- Order: closeAllMediaPresentations, the media-pause JS, unhook delegates and invalidate observations, removeAllUserScripts + removeAllScriptMessageHandlers() on webView.configuration.userContentController (one call replaces the per-name list and covers every world), stopLoading() FIRST, then load about:blank last (or loadHTMLString("", baseURL: nil)) so it is not cancelled. Verify closePane's URL capture still runs before teardown.
- Rewrite the comments in the file's voice.

ACCEPT
- ChordEngineTests: after evicting a pane whose page set an interval that posts to a message handler, no further messages arrive (use an E2E route if a real page is needed); the evicted view's userContentController has no handlers (WKUserContentController offers no list API: assert via a handler added in the test no longer being called).
- Existing split/close/reopen E2E tests pass (SplitViewE2ETests, RestoreAndDownloadsE2ETests).

--------
COMMON CONTEXT (all audit-2026-10-29 tasks)

title: Persist pending data wipes; finish at next launch
description:
WHY
Remove now wipes an extension's data (ExtensionsService.remove -> host.forgetData), so a reinstall starts clean (root cause of Bitwarden's empty popup, 2026-10-29). Also nothing stops a reinstall from loading while the wipe is still running.

- remove(_:) line ~867: appends id to UserDefaults list "extensions.forgetting" (forgettingKey, line 889), starts `forgetting[id] = Task { if await forgetData(of: id) { forgotten(id) } }`.
- forgotten(_:) ~891: removes id from the list.
- forgetLeftOver() ~898: at launch, before any extension loads (start(), line ~200), retries every id still in the list.
- load(_:) line 491: `if let forgetting = forgetting[item.id] { await forgetting.value }` — loading waits for a running wipe.
- forgetData(of:) ~916: chrome.storage via controller.dataRecords/removeData, then origin data from a stand-in context's blank page.

CHORD TODAY

description:

close_reason: Implemented option 3: when more than one tab in a window shares a registrable domain, each row prints the address followed by the page title; a single tab per site keeps the quiet address-only row. Core helper AddressAtRest.repeatedSites with 4 tests; XCUITest testSameSiteTabsShowTitleAfterAddress; full prepush green.

description:

description:
Translate the visible page in place: walk text nodes, title/alt/placeholder/aria-label, all frames and open shadow roots; skip code, inputs and translate=no; detect per-block language; re-translate on DOM mutation; 'Show original' restores. Uses Apple's Translation framework (macOS 15+), which needs on-device language packs and Apple Intelligence on some Macs.

acceptance_criteria: Degrades cleanly where packs/Apple Intelligence are unavailable (clear message, no broken page); code blocks untouched; SPA route changes keep translations consistent; Show Original restores the exact original text; per-site auto-translate of chosen languages.

title: Site-search chips (Search Reddit from a prefix)

Typing a site prefix offers 'Search <site>' as the top suggestion; Tab inserts a chip so the rest of the typing goes to that site. Built-in list of common sites plus OpenSearch discovery from sites the user visits.

title: Import passwords from Chromium browsers
description:
File > Import > Passwords: read a Chromium 'Login Data' SQLite file, decrypt passwords with the '<Browser> Safe Storage' keychain key (AES-CBC, v10 prefix), and write them into ChordSecrets with origin-only matching. Never log secrets, never copy the DB into app support, read a temp copy and delete it.

Search reference: Sources/Search/Import.swift (72 KB, covers many browsers).
design: ChordSecrets + a read-only SQLite reader. Security review needed before merge: temp-file lifetime, memory zeroing of decrypted bytes.
acceptance_criteria: Import from a real Chrome profile produces working fills; wrong/absent keychain key produces a clear error and imports nothing; secrets never appear in logs or crash reports; keychain items are tagged so they can be bulk-removed.
close_reason: Merged to main (d8c6a51). Chromium import with v10/v11 decrypt, temp-copy hygiene, wrapped-key refusal; 149 targeted tests green.

title: Blocked-popup tray with per-site allow
description:
When a popup is refused, keep the last few per tab and show a badge on the tab title. The tray lists them with an Open / Open all action and 'Always allow this site' (per Space). Drop entries when the tab closes.

Search reference: Sources/Search/BlockedPopups.swift.
design: ChordStore: bypass list keyed by site + space. ChordUI: tray in the address field popover. Reuses existing popup plumbing (ADR 018).
acceptance_criteria: Refused popups are listed with URL + opener; opening one respects the existing popup-as-real-web-view behaviour; allow-list persists per site per Space and is revocable in Settings > Sites; private tabs never persist refusals.
close_reason: Merged to main (2fe2024). Popup refusal taxonomy, per-tab tray, per-Space allow/block rules; 172 targeted tests green; full prepush green.

title: What's New card after an update
description:
On the first launch after CFBundleVersion changes, show a one-time card listing what is new, including any new setting that ships off by default. Link to release notes in Settings > About. Dismissal is per build.

Search reference: Sources/Search/WhatsNew.swift.
design: UserDefaults key by bundle version + a sheet. Keep the copy in one file so it is easy to update at release.

title: AppleScript support (read-only tabs, URL, title)
description:
Expose a minimal sdef: application > windows > tabs, current tab, URL, name. Read-only. Private tabs excluded. Requires the Automation permission prompt, and degrades quietly when denied.

Search reference: Sources/Search/Scripting.swift + Search.sdef.
design: ChordApp target: sdef + NSApplication scripting support. No new package.

title: Find a setting (settings search)
description:
One catalog of every settings row: section, title, blurb, icon, search keywords, shortcut. The Settings screen renders from it and a search field (Cmd+F inside Settings) filters to matching rows with the term highlighted and jumps to the section.

Search reference: Sources/Search/SettingsIndex.swift (40 KB).

close_reason: Merged to main (be2929b); settings catalog + search, 12 catalog tests green, package build green.

title: Release media keys when media is idle
description:
After ~10 s of audible silence, mute-and-pause the page's media elements so macOS Now Playing returns to Spotify/Music instead of showing a dead Chord entry. Unmute on real play.

Search reference: Sources/Search/MediaKeys.swift (5 KB).
design: Page script in the isolated world + MPNowPlayingInfoCenter. Small, self-contained, no settings.
acceptance_criteria: Now Playing no longer lists a paused Chord tab after the idle window; playing again restores the entry; no audible blip; works with audio-only pages.
close_reason: Merged to main (e69faf2); prepush green.

title: Probe: which chrome.* APIs WebKit 15.4 already has
description:
Small probe in the test harness that answers, before any port: does our WKWebExtension host support the API surface the Search port relies on? Check chrome.offscreen presence, storage.session presence, userScripts, sidePanel, and whether an injected script survives into a service worker's global scope.

Deliverable: a markdown note appended to the epic with a yes/no line per API, measured on macOS 15.4+ with a scratch MV3 extension. No product code.
design: Scratch extension under Tests/Fixtures; run via the existing debug build; delete the fixture afterwards or keep it as a regression fixture.
acceptance_criteria: Note answers each API with observed evidence (console output or extension error), not inference; conclusion says which shim APIs are actually required vs already present.
close_reason: Probe done. chrome.offscreen ABSENT everywhere (permission silently dropped, createDocument throws). chrome.storage.session present in SW and works; content-script access only after setAccessLevel(TRUSTED_AND_UNTRUSTED_CONTEXTS). userScripts/privacy/sidePanel/tabGroups/notifications/identity/downloads/bookmarks/history absent. Scripting/DNR/alarms/contextMenus/action/cookies/webNavigation/webRequest work. Namespace presence is permission-gated (action is manifest-key-gated); chrome.scripting has 0 enumerable props but works -> feature-detect by typeof. Note + fixture in docs/notes/webkit-ext-api-probe.md and Tests/Fixtures/extension-api-probe/. Docs-only commit acfb14a on spike/webkit-ext-api-probe.

title: WKHTTPCookieStore.cookies(for:) — per-URL cookie inspection in Privacy & Data
description:
Safari 27 adds WKHTTPCookieStore.cookies(for:) — fetch cookies for a specific URL without dumping the whole store. Build a per-site cookie/site-data view in Settings → Privacy & Data, complementing the existing site-permissions UI (Schema v11, per-space). Pairs with 'clear cookies for this site' scoped per data store.

Host is macOS 26.7 with Xcode 27 SDK — available now, no macOS 27 required.

Acceptance: cookie list + per-site clear for the active Space's WKWebsiteDataStore; tests + prepush green.

title: Command bar: URL heuristic polish
description: QoL #4. Sharpen URLInput.looksLikeHost (URLInput.swift:55): add a TLD table so 'foo.grok' type gibberish stops navigating to a DNS error; handle a 'www.' prefix; decide whether single-word intranet hosts ('nas', 'myserver') navigate or search. Deliberately conservative today; the change must not regress the common 'example.com' navigate or multi-token search cases. Needs its own acceptance corpus (like LoginFormClassifier's captured-markup approach): a table of inputs -> expected navigate/search.
design: DESIGN (2026-08-28): Sharpen URLInput.looksLikeHost while staying conservative. 1) TLD table: the final label must be in a curated set of common generic + country TLDs instead of 'any all-letter label' — so 'foo.grok' stops navigating to a DNS error. 2) www prefix: strip a leading 'www.' before judging the TLD, so 'www.example.com' still navigates but 'www.grok' searches. 3) Intranet single-word hosts ('nas','myserver'): kept as SEARCH (conservative) — current behaviour, and 'no navigation for anything that would 100% DNS-fail'. 'localhost' remains the sole single-word navigator. Corpus (captured-style table) in URLInputTests: inputs -> isSearch(true=search,false=navigate). No UI/store/engine change; pure ChordCore.
acceptance_criteria: A corpus table of typed inputs -> navigate|search, incl. 'www x', TLD gibberish, intranet words; all existing URLInputTests still pass; no navigation for anything that would 100% DNS-fail.
close_reason: Replaced 'any all-letter label' with a known-TLD table; strip leading 'www.'; intranet single-words stay search; localhost sole navigator. Corpus table in URLInputTests (11 cases). Tests green (700).

title: Command bar: '@site' site search
description: QoL #5. '@gh swift' searches GitHub, '@so' StackOverflow, etc. Needs a small site registry (name, aliases, search URL template) + URLInput/ranker parsing for a leading '@' token. Developer-oriented; medium build. Independently testable: table of '@alias query' -> engine URL. Do after the ?-prefix lands (same parse layer).
design: DESIGN (2026-08-28): '@site' site search. ChordCore-only, reuses the ?-prefix parse layer. New pure-data SiteRegistry (file ChordCore/SiteRegistry.swift): entries {name, aliases[], urlTemplate with %s} — GitHub(gh), Stack Overflow(so), npm, Wikipedia(w/wiki), YouTube(yt). URLInput.siteSearchQuery(raw:) -> (alias, query)? when the trimmed text starts with '@' and there is a non-empty alias and a non-empty query; nil otherwise (falls through, like '?' alone). CommandBarRanking.fallback checks site-search right after forced-search: '@gh swift' -> .search row with the registry engine URL (via URLInput.search %s substitution); unknown alias -> nil -> normal resolve/search fallback. Title 'Search <Name> for "<query>"'. Unit tests: URLInput.siteSearchQuery table + SiteRegistry alias resolution (case-insensitive) + ranking table '@alias query' -> engine URL + unknown-alias fallback.
acceptance_criteria: '@alias query' opens the registered site's search URL for query; unknown alias falls back to normal search; registry entries are pure data, unit-tested.
close_reason: Added pure-data SiteRegistry + URLInput.siteSearchQuery parse layer; fallback dispatches '@alias query' to the site engine, unknown alias falls back to normal search. Tests green (710).

title: Window event monitors stay installed if their owner skips stop()
description:
SYMPTOM
NSEvent local monitors are installed by SpaceSwipeMonitor (ChordUI/Sidebar/SpaceSwipeMonitor.swift), TitlebarDoubleClickMonitor (ChordUI/TitlebarDoubleClickMonitor.swift), MRUTabKeyMonitor (ChordUI/MRUTabKeyMonitor.swift) and BackSwipeMonitor (ChordEngine/BackSwipeMonitor.swift). Each removes its monitor only in stop(); none does in deinit. RootView (ChordUI/RootView.swift, .onAppear) creates all three window monitors and assigns them to @State without stopping any existing one, and stops them in .onDisappear. If onAppear runs again without a matching onDisappear (window re-attachment, SwiftUI re-creating the view), the previous monitor is dropped while still installed: the app-wide local monitor keeps running on every scroll / key / mouse event for the life of the process (its closure holds self weakly, so it then does nothing but costs a call per event and can never be removed).
Low impact, hardening.

FIX
- In RootView.onAppear, stop() any existing monitor before creating a new one (or guard and reuse it).
- Give each monitor a deinit that removes its NSEvent monitor (these are @MainActor classes: use an isolated deinit if the toolchain allows, else store the token in a nonisolated(unsafe) property and call NSEvent.removeMonitor, which is safe from any thread).

ACCEPT
- Build with warnings as errors; a unit test per monitor that start() then dropping the last reference removes the monitor (observable via a test hook counting active monitors, or by checking the handler is no longer invoked when posting a synthetic event through NSApp.sendEvent).

--------
COMMON CONTEXT (all audit-2026-10-29 tasks)
- Repo: /Users/rizal/perkodingan/webkit-arc-like-browser, base on main at or after 1c4be09. Line numbers are as of 2026-10-29 and drift: search by symbol name.
- Layering (ADR 011): WebKit types stay in Packages/Sources/ChordExtensions and ChordEngine; ChordStore and ChordUI see only WebKit-free protocols (ExtensionHost.swift, WebEngine.swift). A new ExtensionHost/WebEngine method needs a no-op default in the protocol's public extension so test fakes compile (Tests/ChordStoreTests/ExtensionsServiceTests.swift FakeHost, ExtensionModelTests.swift RecordingExtensionHost, ChordTestSupport/Fakes.swift FakeWebEngine).
- Chord is per-Space: WebKitExtensionHost keeps one WKWebExtensionController per Space (controllers[space.id]). Keep it that way.
- Rules: one task = one commit (bd memory one-task-one-commit). Build gate: cd Packages && swift build -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors. Run test targets one at a time with /usr/bin/timeout and pkill -f swiftpm-testing-helper between runs (ChordStoreTests hangs intermittently, x4b): ChordE2ETests, ChordEngineTests, ChordCoreTests, ChordExtensionsTests, ChordStoreTests. Do not push unless asked. After committing, reindex codebase-memory (index_repository, mode full).
- Live check: xcodebuild -project Chord.xcodeproj -scheme Chord -configuration Debug -destination 'platform=macOS' build, then open ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Chord-*/Build/Products/Debug/Chord.app. In this shell `log` is a shell function: use /usr/bin/log show --predicate 'process == "Chord"'. Temporary diagnostics: Log.<category>.notice(...) (NSLog does not reach the unified log here); remove them before committing.
close_reason: Fixed in bd9a89d: the LocalEventMonitor wrapper removes itself on release, and RootView stops existing monitors on re-appear.

title: Command bar: '!' bangs and mid-typing engine switch
description: QoL #6. Firefox/DuckDuckGo-style: '!ddg query' forces a specific search engine, '!w query' Wikipedia, etc. Long tail of the '@site' registry work (#5) - shares the parse layer and registry. Niche; lowest priority in the QoL list.
design: DESIGN (2026-08-28): '!' bangs share the @site parse layer and registry, resolved consistently. Generalize URLInput.siteSearchQuery -> URLInput.dispatchQuery(raw:) accepting BOTH leading '@' and '!' (same alias/query split, same fall-through rules). Extend the pure-data SiteRegistry with search-engine entries so '@' and '!' resolve through the SAME entry(forAlias:) — a conflict (e.g. 'w' in both) lands on the same row, no divergence. New engine entries: Google(g), DuckDuckGo(ddg), Bing(bing), Brave(brave); existing sites unchanged. fallback dispatches '@alias' and '!alias' identically -> .search row with the entry's %s template URL; unknown alias -> normal search. Precedence: '?' forced-search first, then '@'/'!' dispatch, then resolve. Title 'Search <Name> for "<query>"'. Tests: parse table for '!', bang->engine URL table ('!ddg swift'->duckduckgo, '!w x'->wikipedia), consistency ('@gh'=='!gh' same URL), unknown-bang fallback.
acceptance_criteria: '!alias query' searches via the alias's engine; conflicts with '@' resolved consistently; unit-tested alongside #5.
close_reason: Generalized dispatchQuery to '@' and '!'; extended SiteRegistry with engine entries (Google/DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave); '@' and '!' resolve through the same registry. Tests green (714).

title: Passkeys: blocked until paid Apple membership, then system WebAuthn
description:
Goal: passkeys (WebAuthn) work in Chord. Measured 2026-08-28 on the free personal team (74XUPW85K2): Automatic signing refuses com.apple.developer.web-browser ('Entitlement not found and could not be included in profile'), so WKWebView has no platform authenticator and system passkeys are unavailable. Recorded in docs/design/password-vault.md.

Three paths, in order of preference:
1. SYSTEM (recommended once paid): add com.apple.developer.web-browser entitlement, build Release, verify PublicKeyCredential.isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable() returns true on an HTTPS page, then Register/Login on https://webauthn.io/ raises the Touch ID sheet. Works for any site, no extension involved. Unblocks the moment a paid account signs the app.
2. BITWARDEN VAULT: impossible. WebKit's WKWebExtensionController exposes no authenticator hook; Bitwarden's ceremony uses hybrid CTAP2/native-messaging WebKit doesn't implement; its MV3 build also dies at startup (chrome.offscreen). Do not pursue.
3. OWN-CEREMONY SHIM (only subscription-free path, not scheduled): main-world navigator.credentials override (pattern: GeolocationBridge, WebKitEngine.swift:304) bridging to a WebAuthn ceremony in ChordSecrets (WebCrypto: CBOR, COSE, ECDSA/Ed25519). High trust-surface; ADR 016 deferred on security grounds. No entitlements needed.
design: See docs/design/password-vault.md ('No passkeys' bullet) and the path notes in the description.
acceptance_criteria: With a paid membership, com.apple.developer.web-browser is provisioned and isUserVerifyingPlatformAuthenticatorAvailable() returns true on webauthn.io in a Release build.
notes:
2026-10-27: Bitwarden passkey login works in the Search build but not Chord. Search has com.apple.developer.web-browser.public-key-credential in Search.passkeys.entitlements and a 1189-line Sources/Search/Passkeys.swift using ASAuthorizationWebBrowserPublicKeyCredentialManager + conditional-mediation UI (Browser.swift/Tab.swift call sites). Chord's team is 74XUPW85K2 and its entitlements lack the key; Chord also lacks any navigator.credentials bridge. Next spike: add the entitlement and verify codesign/provisioning accepts it before porting the subsystem.
2026-10-29: Correction — Bitwarden VAULT passkeys work without the entitlement (7d37b38): Bitwarden's page script overrides navigator.credentials and does the ceremony in the extension; Chord only had to answer window frames and open its popup as a real window. The entitlement is still needed for system passkeys (iCloud Keychain, phone, security key) and for Bitwarden's fallback to the browser's own WebAuthn, which Search routes to macOS.
